    The top model is ``_1_`` for ColabFold and ``_0_`` for every other engine; the id is
    whatever ``PAE_SAMPLE_REGEX`` makes of that file's path, which is the id
    :func:`structure_entity` gives the structure.
    """
    prefix = f"{engine_dir}/{mode}" if mode else engine_dir
    rank = 1 if engine_dir == "colabfold" else 0
    return sample_from_path(f"{prefix}/{target}/paes/{target}_{rank}_pae.tsv", PAE_SAMPLE_REGEX)


def _parts(path: str) -> list[str]:
    return [p for p in str(path).replace("\\", "/").split("/") if p]


def _engine_index(parts: list[str]) -> int:
    for i in range(len(parts) - 2, -1, -1):
        if parts[i] in ENGINE_DIRS:
            return i
    raise ValueError(f"No proteinfold engine directory in {'/'.join(parts)!r}")


def locate_structure(path: str) -> OutputLocation:
    """Location of ``<engine>[/<mode>]/top_ranked_structures/<target>.pdb``."""
    parts = _parts(path)
    i = _engine_index(parts)
    mode = parts[i + 1] if parts[i + 1] in MODE_DIRS else ""
    target = re.sub(r"\.(?:pdb|cif|mmcif)(?:\.gz)?$", "", parts[-1], flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return OutputLocation(parts[i], mode, target)


def locate_target_file(path: str) -> OutputLocation:
    """Location of a file under ``<engine>[/<mode>]/<target>/`` (any depth below)."""
    parts = _parts(path)
    i = _engine_index(parts)
    rest = parts[i + 1 : -1]
    mode = rest[0] if rest and rest[0] in MODE_DIRS else ""
    below = rest[1:] if mode else rest
    if not below:
        raise ValueError(f"No target directory in {path!r}")
    return OutputLocation(parts[i], mode, below[0])


def raw_blocks(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    """``(source_path, lines)`` per file of a raw-line glob source."""
    blocks = []
    for (path,), block in raw.group_by(SOURCE_PATH_COL, maintain_order=True):
        lines = [str(line) for line in block[RAW_LINE_COL].to_list() if line is not None]
        blocks.append((str(path), lines))
    return blocks


def top_model_residues(raw_pdb: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Residue table of every top-ranked structure, with engine and target.

    Columns: entity, engine, target, chain, position, residue, value (pLDDT on
    a 0-100 scale), category (AlphaFold confidence band), series (the engine,
    suffixed with the chain on multi-chain structures, so one curve per chain).
    """
    frames = []
    for path, lines in raw_blocks(raw_pdb):
        loc = locate_structure(path)
        residues = residues_from_pdb("\n".join(lines) + "\n", loc.entity)
        if residues.is_empty():
            continue
        multi_chain = residues["chain"].n_unique() > 1
        frames.append(
            residues.with_columns(
                pl.lit(loc.engine).alias("engine"),
                pl.lit(loc.target).alias("target"),
                (
                    pl.lit(loc.engine) + pl.lit(" chain ") + pl.col("chain")
                    if multi_chain
                    else pl.lit(loc.engine)
                ).alias("series"),
            )
        )
    columns = {
        "entity": pl.Utf8,
        "engine": pl.Utf8,
        "target": pl.Utf8,
        "chain": pl.Utf8,
        "position": pl.Int64,
        "residue": pl.Utf8,
        "value": pl.Float64,
        "category": pl.Utf8,
        "series": pl.Utf8,
    }
    if not frames:
        return pl.DataFrame(schema=columns)
    return (
        pl.concat(frames, how="vertical")
        .with_columns(plddt_band_expr("value", "category"))
        .select(list(columns))
        .cast(columns)
        .sort(["target", "engine", "chain", "position"])
    )


def _rank_order(labels: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Model rank ids (``rank_0``, ``1``, ...) to 1-based ranks, 1 = top model.

    Engines number their models from 0 (AlphaFold2, ESMFold) or from 1
    (ColabFold); ordering the ids numerically and counting from 1 puts every
    engine on the same scale, with the top-ranked structure at 1.
    """

    def key(label: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
        digits = re.findall(r"\d+", label)
        return (int(digits[-1]) if digits else 0, label)

    return {label: i + 1 for i, label in enumerate(sorted(set(labels), key=key))}


def plddt_long(raw_plddt: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Per-residue pLDDT of every model, from the ``<target>_plddt.tsv`` tables.

    The tables hold one row per residue (``Positions``, 0-based over the chains
    in order) and one ``rank_<k>`` column per model. Columns: entity, engine,
    target, model_rank (1 = top), residue_index (1-based over the chains in
    order), plddt.
    """
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for path, lines in raw_blocks(raw_plddt):
        cells = [line.rstrip("\r").split("\t") for line in lines if line.strip()]
        if len(cells) < 2:
            continue
        header, body = cells[0], cells[1:]
        loc = locate_target_file(path)
        ranks = _rank_order(header[1:])
        for row in body:
            try:
                index = int(float(row[0])) + 1
            except (ValueError, IndexError):
                continue
            for label, cell in zip(header[1:], row[1:], strict=False):
                try:
                    value = float(cell)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "entity": loc.entity,
                        "engine": loc.engine,
                        "target": loc.target,
                        "model_rank": ranks[label],
                        "residue_index": index,
                        "plddt": value,
                    }
                )
    schema = {
        "entity": pl.Utf8,
        "engine": pl.Utf8,
        "target": pl.Utf8,
        "model_rank": pl.Int64,
        "residue_index": pl.Int64,
        "plddt": pl.Float64,
    }
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=schema)


def model_scores_long(raw_scores: pl.DataFrame | None) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """pTM, ipTM and ipSAE per model, from the two-column ``<target>_<metric>.tsv``.

    ``raw_scores`` is the raw scan (``model``, ``score``, ``source_path``);
    empty files (ipTM and ipSAE of a single-chain target) contribute nothing.
    Columns: entity, model_rank, metric (ptm / iptm / ipsae), score.
    """
    schema = {
        "entity": pl.Utf8,
        "model_rank": pl.Int64,
        "metric": pl.Utf8,
        "score": pl.Float64,
    }
    if raw_scores is None or raw_scores.is_empty() or "score" not in raw_scores.columns:
        return pl.DataFrame(schema=schema)
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for (path,), block in raw_scores.group_by(SOURCE_PATH_COL, maintain_order=True):
        match = re.search(r"_(ptm|iptm|ipsae)\.tsv$", str(path))
        if not match or "_chainwise_" in str(path):
            continue
        loc = locate_target_file(str(path))
        block = block.filter(pl.col("model").is_not_null() & pl.col("score").is_not_null())
        ranks = _rank_order([str(m) for m in block["model"].to_list()])
        for model, score in zip(block["model"].to_list(), block["score"].to_list(), strict=True):
            try:
                value = float(score)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                continue
            rows.append(
                {
                    "entity": loc.entity,
                    "model_rank": ranks[str(model)],
                    "metric": match.group(1),
                    "score": value,
                }
            )
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=schema)


def decimate(
    df: pl.DataFrame, by: list[str], x: str, y: str, max_points: int = 200
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """At most ``max_points`` rows per ``by`` group: means over equal x windows.

    Groups already under the cap pass unchanged. ``x`` becomes the window's
    middle position (rounded), ``y`` its mean; other columns keep their first
    value in the window.
    """
    if df.is_empty():
        return df
    sizes = df.group_by(by).len()
    if int(sizes["len"].max() or 0) <= max_points:
        return df
    others = [c for c in df.columns if c not in {*by, x, y}]
    ordered = df.sort([*by, x]).with_columns(
        (pl.int_range(pl.len()).over(by) * max_points // pl.len().over(by)).alias("_window")
    )
    return (
        ordered.group_by([*by, "_window"], maintain_order=True)
        .agg(
            pl.col(x).mean().round(0).cast(df.schema[x]).alias(x),
            pl.col(y).mean().cast(df.schema[y]).alias(y),
            *[pl.col(c).first() for c in others],
        )
        .select(df.columns)
    )
files.depictio/recipes/lib/qualimap_raw.py:
"""Read Qualimap BamQC's raw per-position tables, which never name their sample.

Qualimap BamQC publishes a per-sample directory (``<sample>_stats/``,
``<sample>_rmdup_stats/`` after deduplication, ``<sample>/`` on some wrappers)
holding ``genome_results.txt`` and a ``raw_data_qualimapReport/`` subdirectory
(``raw_data/`` on Qualimap builds before 2.2) with one plain table per plot:
``coverage_across_reference.txt``, ``coverage_histogram.txt``,
``genome_fraction_coverage.txt`` and seven more.

Every one of those tables has the same shape: a single ``#``-prefixed header
line, then tab-separated numeric columns. None of them carries the sample name,
which lives only in the directory two or three levels up, so the recipes that
read them all need the same two things and get them here:

* :func:`sample_from_report_path`, the sample id, walking past whichever
  ``raw_data*`` directory the Qualimap build wrote.
* :func:`split_columns`, the tab split, applied to the raw one-line-per-row
  scan the data collections use (a separator the tables cannot contain, so
  nothing splits before the recipe sees it and a table's column count is not
  baked into the scan).

Shared here rather than copied because four catalog recipes in one tool need
exactly this, and recipes may not import each other.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import polars as pl

#: Column holding one full line of the table (the raw DC scans with a separator
#: the file cannot contain, so every line lands in this single column).
RAW_LINE_COL = "raw"
#: Column carrying the table's path (``include_file_paths`` on the raw DC).
SOURCE_PATH_COL = "source_path"

#: Directories Qualimap interposes between the sample directory and the table.
_RAW_DIRS = frozenset({"raw_data_qualimapreport", "raw_data"})

#: Trailing underscore-separated tokens of the sample directory that describe a
#: processing stage rather than the sample: Qualimap's own ``_stats`` suffix,
#: plus the dedupper stage a pipeline ran before BamQC (Picard MarkDuplicates
#: writes ``_rmdup``, DeDup writes ``_dedup``).
_STAGE_TOKENS = frozenset({"stats", "rmdup", "dedup", "results", "bamqc"})


def sample_from_report_path(source_path: str) -> str:
    """The sample id a Qualimap table belongs to, read off its directory.

    Never returns an empty string: a directory made entirely of stage tokens is
    handed back as it came, because dropping it would merge two samples.
    """
    parts = str(source_path).replace("\\", "/").split("/")[:-1]
    while parts and parts[-1].lower() in _RAW_DIRS:
        parts.pop()
    dirname = parts[-1] if parts else ""
    tokens = dirname.split("_")
    while len(tokens) > 1 and tokens[-1].lower() in _STAGE_TOKENS:
        tokens.pop()
    return "_".join(tokens) or dirname


def split_columns(raw: pl.DataFrame, names: list[str], *, recipe: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """``sample`` plus one Utf8 column per name, split off the raw line column.

    Rows shorter than ``names`` come back with nulls rather than raising: a
    Qualimap table truncated by an interrupted run should cost its rows, not
    the whole collection.
    """
    if raw.is_empty():
        raise ValueError(f"{recipe}: the scanned tables are empty")
    for column in (RAW_LINE_COL, SOURCE_PATH_COL):
        if column not in raw.columns:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{recipe}: no {column} column, the data collection must scan one "
                f"line per row with include_file_paths: source_path"
            )

    fields = pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.strip_chars().str.split("\t")
    return (
        raw.filter(pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).is_not_null() & (pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.len_chars() > 0))
        .filter(~pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.starts_with("#"))
        .with_columns(fields.alias("__fields"))
        .select(
            pl.col(SOURCE_PATH_COL)
            .map_elements(sample_from_report_path, return_dtype=pl.Utf8)
            .alias("sample"),
            *[
                pl.col("__fields").list.get(i, null_on_oob=True).str.strip_chars().alias(name)
                for i, name in enumerate(names)
            ],
        )
    )


#: Marker opening the per-contig block that closes ``genome_results.txt``.
CONTIG_MARKER = ">>>>>>> Coverage per contig"

#: Columns of :func:`contig_coverage_block`, in the order the block writes them.
CONTIG_BLOCK_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "sample": pl.Utf8,
    "chromosome": pl.Utf8,
    "length": pl.Int64,
    "mapped_bases": pl.Int64,
    "mean_coverage": pl.Float64,
    "coverage_std": pl.Float64,
}


def _int_or_none(text: str | None) -> int | None:
    try:
        return int(float(text))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _float_or_none(text: str | None) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(text)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def contig_coverage_block(raw: pl.DataFrame, *, recipe: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per (sample, contig) from the ``Coverage per contig`` block, in file order.

    ``raw`` is the one-line-per-row scan of ``genome_results.txt``. The block lists
    every reference sequence as contig, length, mapped bases, mean depth and depth
    standard deviation, tab-separated and leading-tab indented. A line whose length
    does not parse is skipped outright; the other three numbers are null when they
    are missing or unparsable, so each caller decides whether a contig without a
    depth is worth a row. Rows keep the file's order, which is the reference order
    Qualimap concatenated its genome-wide axis in.

    Raises ``ValueError`` when the scan is empty or lacks the two columns. Returns
    an empty frame (with :data:`CONTIG_BLOCK_SCHEMA`) when no report carries the
    block, which Qualimap omits on a single-sequence reference.
    """
    if raw.is_empty():
        raise ValueError(f"{recipe}: the scanned reports are empty")
    for column in (RAW_LINE_COL, SOURCE_PATH_COL):
        if column not in raw.columns:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{recipe}: no {column} column, the data collection must scan one "
                f"line per row with include_file_paths: source_path"
            )

    rows: list[dict] = []
    for (path,), group in raw.group_by([SOURCE_PATH_COL], maintain_order=True):
        sample = sample_from_report_path(str(path))
        in_block = False
        for line in group[RAW_LINE_COL].to_list():
            text = line or ""
            if text.startswith(CONTIG_MARKER):
                in_block = True
                continue
            if not in_block:
                continue
            if text.startswith(">>>>>>>"):
                break
            fields = [f for f in text.split("\t") if f]
            if len(fields) < 2:
                continue
            length = _int_or_none(fields[1])
            if length is None:
                continue
            rows.append(
                {
                    "sample": sample,
                    "chromosome": fields[0],
                    "length": length,
                    "mapped_bases": _int_or_none(fields[2]) if len(fields) > 2 else None,
                    "mean_coverage": _float_or_none(fields[3]) if len(fields) > 3 else None,
                    "coverage_std": _float_or_none(fields[4]) if len(fields) > 4 else None,
                }
            )
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=CONTIG_BLOCK_SCHEMA)

"""Read a QUAST transposed report, whatever QUAST called its columns.

QUAST writes the same table for a whole assembly and for a single bin, one row
per assembly in `transposed_report.tsv` (and in the `*-quast_summary.tsv`
nf-core/mag aggregates per binning run). Its column names carry units and
comparison operators (`# contigs (>= 1000 bp)`, `GC (%)`, `# N's per 100 kbp`),
which change between QUAST versions and between the `quast` and `metaquast`
front-ends, so nothing may match them literally.

Names are folded to `#` -> `n`, non-alphanumerics -> `_` before matching, which
turns `# contigs (>= 1000 bp)` into `n_contigs_1000_bp` and `GC (%)` into
`gc`. The two families that vary with QUAST's `--contig-thresholds` are matched
by pattern rather than by name, so a run configured with other thresholds still
reads.

Shared by the `quast` catalog outputs (whole assemblies, per-bin summaries and
the contig-length ladder) because they parse one file shape three ways and
recipes may not import each other.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import polars as pl

#: `# contigs (>= 1000 bp)` and `Total length (>= 1000 bp)` after folding.
_N_CONTIGS_THRESHOLD_RE = re.compile(r"^n_contigs_(?P<bp>\d+)_bp$")
_TOTAL_LENGTH_THRESHOLD_RE = re.compile(r"^total_length_(?P<bp>\d+)_bp$")

#: Output column -> the folded QUAST name it comes from. The unqualified
#: `# contigs` / `Total length` are QUAST's own headline numbers (contigs past
#: its `--min-contig` cut), not a threshold row.
SCALAR_COLUMNS: dict[str, str] = {
    "n_contigs": "n_contigs",
    "largest_contig": "largest_contig",
    "total_length": "total_length",
    "gc_percent": "gc",
    "n50": "n50",
    "n75": "n75",
    "l50": "l50",
    "l75": "l75",
    "ns_per_100_kbp": "n_ns_per_100_kbp",
    "predicted_rrna_genes": "n_predicted_rrna_genes",
}

#: Which of those are counts rather than measurements.
INTEGER_COLUMNS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {"n_contigs", "largest_contig", "total_length", "n50", "n75", "l50", "l75"}
)


def fold(name: str) -> str:
    """QUAST's column name reduced to something stable across its versions."""
    folded = str(name).strip().lower().replace("#", "n").replace("'", "")
    folded = re.sub(r"[^0-9a-z]+", "_", folded)
    return folded.strip("_")


def column_map(columns: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Folded name -> original name, first spelling wins."""
    mapping: dict[str, str] = {}
    for column in columns:
        mapping.setdefault(fold(column), column)
    return mapping


def scalar_expressions(columns: list[str]) -> list[pl.Expr]:
    """One cast expression per entry of `SCALAR_COLUMNS`, null when absent.

    `# predicted rRNA genes` is left as text on purpose: QUAST writes it as
    `23 + 20 part`, so a cast would silently drop the partial hits.
    """
    mapping = column_map(columns)
    expressions: list[pl.Expr] = []
    for alias, folded in SCALAR_COLUMNS.items():
        original = mapping.get(folded)
        if original is None:
            dtype = pl.Utf8 if alias == "predicted_rrna_genes" else pl.Float64
            if alias in INTEGER_COLUMNS:
                dtype = pl.Int64
            expressions.append(pl.lit(None, dtype=dtype).alias(alias))
        elif alias == "predicted_rrna_genes":
            expressions.append(pl.col(original).cast(pl.Utf8).alias(alias))
        elif alias in INTEGER_COLUMNS:
            expressions.append(
                pl.col(original)
                .cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
                .cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
                .alias(alias)
            )
        else:
            expressions.append(pl.col(original).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).alias(alias))
    return expressions


def label_parts(label: pl.Expr) -> tuple[pl.Expr, pl.Expr]:
    """``<assembler>-<sample>`` split into (assembler, sample) expressions.

    nf-core/mag labels every assembly it hands to QUAST that way. A label with
    no dash keeps both parts null, and a part that is empty (a leading or
    trailing dash) is null rather than "", so a filter on either column never
    offers a blank value.
    """
    text = label.cast(pl.Utf8)
    has_dash = text.str.contains("-", literal=True)
    assembler = text.str.extract(r"^([^-]*)-", 1)
    sample = text.str.extract(r"^[^-]*-(.*)$", 1)
    return (
        pl.when(has_dash & (assembler.str.len_chars() > 0)).then(assembler).otherwise(None),
        pl.when(has_dash & (sample.str.len_chars() > 0)).then(sample).otherwise(None),
    )


def threshold_columns(columns: list[str]) -> list[tuple[int, str | None, str | None]]:
    """Every `--contig-thresholds` step present, as (bp, n_contigs_col, total_length_col)."""
    mapping = column_map(columns)
    counts: dict[int, str] = {}
    lengths: dict[int, str] = {}
    for folded, original in mapping.items():
        match = _N_CONTIGS_THRESHOLD_RE.match(folded)
        if match:
            counts[int(match.group("bp"))] = original
            continue
        match = _TOTAL_LENGTH_THRESHOLD_RE.match(folded)
        if match:
            lengths[int(match.group("bp"))] = original
    steps = sorted(set(counts) | set(lengths))
    return [(bp, counts.get(bp), lengths.get(bp)) for bp in steps]
files.depictio/recipes/lib/repeatmasker_tbl.py:
"""Parse RepeatMasker ``.tbl`` summaries.

RepeatMasker closes every run with a fixed-width summary table::

    ==================================================
    file name: genome.fna
    sequences:           177
    total length:  225250884 bp  (223937270 bp excl N/X-runs)
    GC level:         32.53 %
    bases masked:   38935182 bp ( 17.29 %)
    ==================================================
                   number of      length   percentage
                   elements*    occupied  of sequence
    --------------------------------------------------
    Retroelements        18689      2803554 bp    1.24 %
       SINEs:              335        41217 bp    0.02 %
       ...
         L2/CR1/Rex       2394       171922 bp    0.08 %
    ...
    Total interspersed repeats:    27682653 bp   12.29 %

The header gives the assembly totals; the body one line per repeat class, its
depth in the hierarchy given by the indent (none for a top class, three spaces
for a class of retroelement or transposon, five for a family). A name can wrap
onto the next line (``Other (Mirage,`` then ``P-element, Transib)``).

Every body line is read with a ``rank``:

* ``Class``: the classes that partition what was masked (SINEs, LINEs, LTR
  elements and Penelope under the retroelements, then DNA transposons,
  rolling-circles, unclassified, small RNA, satellites, simple repeats and low
  complexity), the ones a composition bar stacks;
* ``Family``: the families under a class (L2/CR1/Rex, Gypsy/DIRS1, Tc1-IS630-Pogo...);
* ``Summary``: the two lines that add classes up (Retroelements, Total
  interspersed repeats), never stacked with the rest.

Shared by the catalog ``repeatmasker`` outputs (recipes may not import each other).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

import polars as pl

RAW_LINE_COL = "raw_line"
SOURCE_PATH_COL = "source_path"

READ_KWARGS: dict = {
    "separator": "\x1e",
    "has_header": False,
    "new_columns": [RAW_LINE_COL],
    "quote_char": None,
    "infer_schema_length": 0,
}

CLASS_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "genome": pl.Utf8,
    "repeat_class": pl.Utf8,
    "parent_class": pl.Utf8,
    "rank": pl.Utf8,
    "class_order": pl.Int64,
    "elements": pl.Int64,
    "length_bp": pl.Int64,
    "genome_pct": pl.Float64,
}

SUMMARY_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "genome": pl.Utf8,
    "sequences": pl.Int64,
    "total_length": pl.Int64,
    "length_excl_n": pl.Int64,
    "gc_pct": pl.Float64,
    "masked_bp": pl.Int64,
    "masked_pct": pl.Float64,
}

#: Top-level lines that add classes up rather than being one.
SUMMARY_LINES = frozenset({"retroelements", "total interspersed repeats"})

#: One body line, stripped: name, element count (absent on the totals), length, share.
_BODY = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<name>\S.*?):?\s+(?:(?P<elements>\d+)\s+)?(?P<length>\d+)\s+bp\s+"
    r"(?P<pct>[\d.]+)\s*%\s*$"
)
_HEADER_NUM = re.compile(r"^(?P<key>[a-zA-Z ]+):\s*(?P<rest>.*)$")
_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\.tbl$")


def genome_of(source_path: str) -> str:
    """``repeatmasker/A/A.tbl`` -> ``A``."""
    return _SUFFIX.sub("", PurePosixPath(str(source_path).replace("\\", "/")).name)


def _first_int(text: str) -> int | None:
    match = re.search(r"\d+", text)
    return int(match.group(0)) if match else None


def _header(lines: list[str]) -> dict:
    out: dict = {"sequences": None, "total_length": None, "length_excl_n": None}
    out.update({"gc_pct": None, "masked_bp": None, "masked_pct": None})
    for line in lines:
        match = _HEADER_NUM.match(line.strip())
        if match is None:
            continue
        key, rest = match.group("key").strip().lower(), match.group("rest")
        if key == "sequences":
            out["sequences"] = _first_int(rest)
        elif key == "total length":
            numbers = re.findall(r"(\d+)\s*bp", rest)
            out["total_length"] = int(numbers[0]) if numbers else None
            out["length_excl_n"] = int(numbers[1]) if len(numbers) > 1 else None
        elif key == "gc level":
            pct = re.search(r"[\d.]+", rest)
            out["gc_pct"] = float(pct.group(0)) if pct else None
        elif key == "bases masked":
            out["masked_bp"] = _first_int(rest)
            pct = re.search(r"\(\s*([\d.]+)\s*%", rest)
            out["masked_pct"] = float(pct.group(1)) if pct else None
    return out


def _lines_by_file(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    grouped = raw.group_by(SOURCE_PATH_COL, maintain_order=True).agg(pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL))
    return [(path, [str(x) for x in lines if x is not None]) for path, lines in grouped.iter_rows()]


def _level(indent: int) -> int:
    """Hierarchy level of a body line from its indent: 0 top, 1 class, 2 family, 3 below."""
    if indent == 0:
        return 0
    if indent <= 3:
        return 1
    return 2 if indent <= 5 else 3


def parse_classes(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Every repeat class line of every table, with its rank and parent class."""
    rows: list[list] = []
    for path, lines in _lines_by_file(raw):
        genome = genome_of(path)
        in_body, order = False, 0
        # (indent, name) of the open lines above the current one.
        stack: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
        last: list | None = None
        for line in lines:
            text = line.rstrip()
            if text.startswith("-----"):
                in_body = True
                continue
            if not in_body or not text.strip():
                continue
            if text.startswith("====="):
                break
            indent = len(text) - len(text.lstrip())
            match = _BODY.match(text.strip())
            if match is None:
                # The wrapped tail of the previous name ("P-element, Transib)").
                if last is not None and indent > 0:
                    last[1] = f"{last[1]} {text.strip()}"
                continue
            name = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", match.group("name")).strip().rstrip(":").strip()
            # RepeatMasker's indents drift by a space within a level (CRE/SLACS
            # sits at 4, its siblings at 5), so they are bucketed into levels.
            level = _level(indent)
            while stack and stack[-1][0] >= level:
                stack.pop()
            top = stack[0][1] if stack else None
            parent = stack[-1][1] if stack else None
            if indent == 0:
                rank = "Summary" if name.lower() in SUMMARY_LINES else "Class"
            elif top is not None and top.lower() in SUMMARY_LINES and len(stack) == 1:
                # SINEs, LINEs, LTR elements, Penelope: the classes the
                # retroelement line adds up.
                rank = "Class"
            else:
                rank = "Family"
            order += 1
            elements = match.group("elements")
            last = [
                genome,
                name,
                parent,
                rank,
                order,
                int(elements) if elements is not None else None,
                int(match.group("length")),
                float(match.group("pct")),
            ]
            rows.append(last)
            stack.append((level, name))
    return pl.DataFrame([tuple(r) for r in rows], schema=CLASS_SCHEMA, orient="row")


def parse_summaries(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The header totals of every table, one row per assembly."""
    rows = []
    for path, lines in _lines_by_file(raw):
        head = _header(lines)
        if head["total_length"] is None and head["masked_bp"] is None:
            continue
        rows.append({"genome": genome_of(path), **head})
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=SUMMARY_SCHEMA)
files.depictio/recipes/lib/sample_hub.py:
"""Carry a run's design columns from the ``samples`` hub onto a recipe's output.

A template may declare a sample sheet under the repo-wide ``samples`` tag, and
when it does, an output is far more useful coloured by the factor the run
compares than by the sample id. The hub is optional though, and a template that
declares one need not declare every design column, so the columns have to exist
either way: a figure bound to ``treatment`` must find a ``treatment`` column,
null everywhere, rather than fail to build.

Shared here rather than copied because more than one recipe joins the same hub
the same way, and recipes may not import one another.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

import polars as pl

HUB_KEY = "sample_id"


def annotate_from_hub(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    samples: pl.DataFrame | None,
    columns: Sequence[str],
    *,
    left_on: str = HUB_KEY,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Left-join the hub's design ``columns``, null-filling the absent ones.

    ``left_on`` names ``frame``'s own sample column; the hub is always keyed on
    ``sample_id``.
    """
    carried = (
        [c for c in columns if c in samples.columns]
        if samples is not None and not samples.is_empty() and HUB_KEY in samples.columns
        else []
    )
    if carried:
        frame = frame.join(
            samples.select(HUB_KEY, *carried).unique(subset=HUB_KEY),
            left_on=left_on,
            right_on=HUB_KEY,
            how="left",
        )
    return frame.with_columns(
        *[
            (pl.col(column) if column in carried else pl.lit(None)).cast(pl.Utf8).alias(column)
            for column in columns
        ]
    )
files.depictio/recipes/lib/sample_ids.py:
"""Recover a sample id from an alignment-derived file or BAM name.

The ChIP-family pipelines publish per-sample QC beside a BAM whose name records
every stage it went through, and different tools quote a different amount of it:

    GM12878_STD_R1.mLb.mkD.ccurve.txt          preseq, atacseq
    EZH2_IP_NTKO_R1.ccurve.txt                 preseq, chipseq
    GM12878_OMNI_R1.mLb.clN                    deepTools Sample column, atacseq
    h3k4me3_R1.target.markdup.sorted.bam       deepTools Sample column, cutandrun

All four name the same thing: a sample of the samplesheet. Trimming them with a
regex anchored at the end is fragile — the stage tokens and the format suffix
interleave differently per pipeline, and a single pass leaves whichever half it
did not match. So the name is split on ``.`` and trailing tokens are dropped
while they are known stage or format words, which converges regardless of order
and never eats a token it does not recognise.

Shared here rather than copied because three recipes in two tools need exactly
this, and recipes may not import each other.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

#: Trailing dot-separated tokens that describe a processing stage or a file
#: format rather than the sample. Compared lower-cased.
STAGE_TOKENS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        # formats
        "txt",
        "tab",
        "tsv",
        "csv",
        "bam",
        "bed",
        # tool-written suffixes
        "ccurve",
        "c_curve",
        "lc_extrap",
        "plotfingerprint",
        "plotprofile",
        "plotpca",
        "plotcorrelation",
        "qcmetrics",
        "raw",
        "mat",
        # alignment stages: chipseq / atacseq merged library and replicate
        # levels, and the filtering steps applied at each
        "mlb",
        "mrp",
        "mkd",
        "cln",
        "clt",
        # cutandrun
        "target",
        "spikein",
        "markdup",
        "sorted",
        "dedup",
    }
)

#: Alignment stages rnavar and sarek write into their samtools report names
#: (`GM12878_REP1.aligned.stats`, `GM12878_REP1.md.stats`). Kept out of
#: ``STAGE_TOKENS`` because that list also drives the CLI's MultiQC sample
#: mapping, where `S1_2.md` must stay `S1_2` and not lose its read number:
#: only the samtools recipes that read these reports pass them as ``extra``.
ALIGNMENT_STAGE_TOKENS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"aligned", "md"})


def strip_stage_suffixes(name: str, extra: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> str:
    """The sample id inside a published file or BAM name.

    Never returns an empty string: a name made entirely of stage tokens is
    handed back as it came, because dropping it would silently merge samples.
    """
    stem = str(name).replace("\\", "/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    tokens = stem.split(".")
    while len(tokens) > 1 and (tokens[-1].lower() in STAGE_TOKENS or tokens[-1].lower() in extra):
        tokens.pop()
    return ".".join(tokens)
files.depictio/recipes/lib/sarek_units.py:
"""Who a nf-core/sarek call belongs to: a sample, or a tumour/normal pair.

sarek calls variants per *unit*. A unit is one sample (``S1``) or, for the callers
that read a tumour against its matched normal, a pair named ``<tumour>_vs_<normal>``.
Every published file carries the unit in its name, never a column, so the recipes
that read calls ask this module what a unit is:

``germline``
    a single sample whose samplesheet ``status`` is 0 (normal), or one the sheet does
    not describe (the graceful default of a run read from ``variantcalled.csv`` alone);
``tumour_only``
    a single sample with ``status`` 1, called without a matched normal;
``paired``
    a ``<tumour>_vs_<normal>`` unit.

The hub (``samples``) is the only place the status lives, so the split is made from it.
The three classes are never mixed on one scale: the germline tabs read ``germline``,
the Somatic tabs read the other two.

Also here: ``design``, the per-patient label the hub carries (``Paired``,
``Germline only``, ``Tumour-only``), from the same status column.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import polars as pl

#: A paired somatic caller names its unit after the pair: ``<tumour>_vs_<normal>``.
PAIR_SEP = "_vs_"

GERMLINE = "germline"
TUMOUR_ONLY = "tumour_only"
PAIRED = "paired"
UNIT_TYPES = (GERMLINE, TUMOUR_ONLY, PAIRED)

#: The hub's per-patient design labels.
DESIGN_PAIRED = "Paired"
DESIGN_GERMLINE = "Germline only"
DESIGN_TUMOUR_ONLY = "Tumour-only"

#: Schema of :func:`unit_frame`.
UNIT_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "unit": pl.Utf8,
    "unit_type": pl.Utf8,
    "patient": pl.Utf8,
    "sample": pl.Utf8,
    "normal": pl.Utf8,
}


def is_pair(unit: str | None) -> bool:
    """True for a ``<tumour>_vs_<normal>`` unit name."""
    return bool(unit) and PAIR_SEP in str(unit)


def split_pair(unit: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """``(tumour, normal)`` of a pair, ``(unit, None)`` of a single sample."""
    tumour, sep, normal = unit.partition(PAIR_SEP)
    return (tumour, normal) if sep else (unit, None)


def design_label(statuses: list[int | None]) -> str:
    """The design of one patient from the status of its samples.

    A tumour and a normal make a pair; tumours alone are tumour-only; anything else
    (normals, or samples whose status is unknown) is germline only, the behaviour of
    a run that never told sarek about tumours.
    """
    has_tumour = any(s == 1 for s in statuses)
    has_normal = any(s != 1 for s in statuses)
    if has_tumour and has_normal:
        return DESIGN_PAIRED
    if has_tumour:
        return DESIGN_TUMOUR_ONLY
    return DESIGN_GERMLINE


def unit_frame(units: list[str | None] | pl.Series, hub: pl.DataFrame | None) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per distinct unit: its type, patient, tumour sample and normal sample.

    ``sample`` is the sample whose reads carry the call: the sample itself for a
    single-sample unit, the tumour of a pair. ``normal`` is the pair's normal, null
    otherwise. ``hub`` is the ``samples`` collection (``sample_id``, ``patient``,
    ``status``); without it every single sample is ``germline`` and the patient is
    unknown.
    """
    names = sorted(
        {str(u) for u in (units.to_list() if isinstance(units, pl.Series) else units) if u}
    )
    parts = pl.col("unit").str.splitn(PAIR_SEP, 2)
    df = pl.DataFrame({"unit": names}, schema={"unit": pl.Utf8}).with_columns(
        parts.struct.field("field_0").alias("sample"),
        parts.struct.field("field_1").alias("normal"),
    )
    if hub is not None and not hub.is_empty() and "sample_id" in hub.columns:
        lookup = hub.select(
            pl.col("sample_id").cast(pl.Utf8).alias("sample"),
            (pl.col("patient") if "patient" in hub.columns else pl.lit(None))
            .cast(pl.Utf8)
            .alias("patient"),
            (pl.col("status") if "status" in hub.columns else pl.lit(None))
            .cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
            .alias("_status"),
        ).unique(subset="sample", keep="first")
        df = df.join(lookup, on="sample", how="left")
    else:
        df = df.with_columns(
            pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("patient"),
            pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Int64).alias("_status"),
        )
    return df.select(
        "unit",
        pl.when(pl.col("normal").is_not_null())
        .then(pl.lit(PAIRED))
        .when(pl.col("_status") == 1)
        .then(pl.lit(TUMOUR_ONLY))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(GERMLINE))
        .alias("unit_type"),
        "patient",
        "sample",
        "normal",
    )


def keep_unit_types(
    df: pl.DataFrame, hub: pl.DataFrame | None, *types: str, unit_col: str = "sample"
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The rows of ``df`` whose ``unit_col`` is a unit of one of ``types``."""
    if df.is_empty():
        return df
    units = unit_frame(df[unit_col], hub).filter(pl.col("unit_type").is_in(types))
    return df.join(units.select(pl.col("unit").alias(unit_col)), on=unit_col, how="inner")
files.depictio/recipes/lib/scrnaseq_panels.py:
"""Gene panels and marker-panel resolution the single-cell recipes share.

Two things live here because several recipes read them:

* the reader's marker panel. It is never hardcoded: a run passes it as the
  optional ``MARKER_PANEL`` template variable (a comma-separated list of gene
  symbols, forwarded to the recipes as the ``marker_panel`` transform param),
  and when it is absent, or none of its genes is in the run's reference, the
  recipes fall back to the top markers of every graph-based cluster from
  ``cellranger_diffexp``. The wide cell x gene table
  (``cellranger/cell_expression.py``) and its melted companion
  (``cellranger/cell_expression_long.py``) both resolve the panel through
  :func:`resolve_marker_panel`, so a mouse or a non-blood run gets a panel built
  from its own clusters instead of an empty one.
* the two Tirosh cell-cycle sets the cell-cycle scorer
  (``cellranger/cell_cycle.py``) reads. They are human gene symbols; on another
  organism the intersection is empty and every cell's phase degrades to NA.

Gene names are SYMBOLS, matched against the filtered matrix's ``features.tsv.gz``
second column. Nothing here is required to be present: a recipe intersects a
list with the features the run actually carries and works with what is left.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping

import polars as pl

#: transform param carrying the ``MARKER_PANEL`` template variable
MARKER_PANEL_PARAM = "marker_panel"

#: the clustering the data-derived fallback reads its markers from
GRAPHCLUST_RESOLUTION = "graphclust"


def parse_marker_panel(value: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Split a ``MARKER_PANEL`` value into gene symbols, in order, deduplicated.

    Accepts commas, semicolons or whitespace as separators. An unset variable
    reaches a recipe either as ``None``, an empty string or the literal
    ``{MARKER_PANEL}`` placeholder the template engine leaves behind; all three
    mean "no panel".
    """
    if not value:
        return ()
    tokens = value.replace(";", ",").replace("\n", ",").replace("\t", ",").split(",")
    genes: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for token in tokens:
        for gene in token.split():
            gene = gene.strip().strip("'\"")
            if not gene or "{" in gene or "}" in gene or gene in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(gene)
            genes.append(gene)
    return tuple(genes)


def marker_panel_from_params(params: Mapping[str, str] | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The reader's panel from a recipe's transform params, empty when unset."""
    if not params:
        return ()
    return parse_marker_panel(params.get(MARKER_PANEL_PARAM))


def top_markers_per_cluster(diffexp: pl.DataFrame | None, per_cluster: int) -> list[str]:
    """The ``per_cluster`` best-ranked markers of every graph-based cluster.

    Ordered by rank first, then cluster, so a cap applied by the caller keeps
    the top marker of every cluster before the second marker of any. Empty when
    the diffexp table is missing or lacks the expected columns.
    """
    if diffexp is None or diffexp.is_empty():
        return []
    if not {"gene", "rank_in_cluster", "cluster"} <= set(diffexp.columns):
        return []
    markers = diffexp
    if "resolution" in markers.columns:
        graph = markers.filter(pl.col("resolution") == GRAPHCLUST_RESOLUTION)
        if not graph.is_empty():
            markers = graph
    markers = markers.filter(pl.col("rank_in_cluster") <= per_cluster).sort(
        ["rank_in_cluster", "cluster"]
    )
    return _dedupe(markers["gene"].cast(pl.Utf8).to_list())


def resolve_marker_panel(
    params: Mapping[str, str] | None,
    diffexp: pl.DataFrame | None,
    available: Iterable[str],
    per_cluster: int,
    cap: int,
) -> list[str]:
    """The genes a per-cell marker tile shows, never empty when ``available`` is not.

    1. the reader's ``MARKER_PANEL``, restricted to genes the run carries;
    2. otherwise the top ``per_cluster`` markers of each graph-based cluster;
    3. otherwise the first ``cap`` available genes, in their given order.
    """
    available_list = [gene for gene in available if gene]
    available_set = set(available_list)
    panel = [gene for gene in marker_panel_from_params(params) if gene in available_set]
    if not panel:
        panel = [
            gene for gene in top_markers_per_cluster(diffexp, per_cluster) if gene in available_set
        ]
    if not panel:
        panel = available_list
    return panel[:cap]


def _dedupe(names: Iterable[str | None]) -> list[str]:
    seen: set[str] = set()
    ordered: list[str] = []
    for name in names:
        if name and name not in seen:
            seen.add(name)
            ordered.append(name)
    return ordered

#: two renamed symbols spelled both ways so an older and a newer reference both hit.

files.depictio/recipes/lib/secondary_structure:
"""S4PRED / PSIPRED secondary-structure predictions (``.ss2``) as a residue table.

nf-core/proteinannotator runs S4PRED and publishes one ``.ss2`` file per sequence
in PSIPRED's VFORMAT::

    # PSIPRED VFORMAT (S4PRED V1.2.1)

       1 M C   0.999  0.001  0.000
       2 K H   0.210  0.760  0.030

that is ``position residue state P(coil) P(helix) P(strand)`` with the state one
of ``C``, ``H``, ``E``.

:func:`parse_ss2` yields exactly the columns of the s4pred catalog recipe
(``depictio/catalog/s4pred/secondary_structure.py``: ``OUTPUT_SCHEMA``, the
``STATES`` names, the ``value`` rule and the sort order), so a recipe can call it
instead of repeating the split. :func:`segments` turns the per-residue states
into the runs a secondary-structure track draws.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

import polars as pl

#: Columns of :func:`parse_ss2`; the s4pred recipe's ``OUTPUT_SCHEMA`` is built from them.
SS2_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "entity": pl.Utf8,
    "sample": pl.Utf8,
    "position": pl.Int64,
    "residue": pl.Utf8,
    "ss_code": pl.Utf8,
    "category": pl.Utf8,
    "value": pl.Float64,
    "p_coil": pl.Float64,
    "p_helix": pl.Float64,
    "p_strand": pl.Float64,
}

#: Predicted state code -> its name in the ``category`` column.
STATES = {"H": "Helix", "E": "Strand", "C": "Coil"}


def _to_int(token: str | None) -> int | None:
    try:
        return int(token) if token is not None else None
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _to_float(token: str | None) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(token) if token is not None else None
    except ValueError:
        return None


def parse_ss2(text: str, entity: str, sample: str | None = None) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per residue line of an ``.ss2`` file.

    Comment (``#``) and blank lines are skipped, as is any line whose first field is
    not an integer. ``position`` is the one written in the file (1-based).
    ``category`` names the called state (Helix, Strand, Coil; null for any other
    code) and ``value`` is the probability of that state: ``p_helix`` for ``H``,
    ``p_strand`` for ``E`` and ``p_coil`` otherwise, like the recipe. ``sample``
    defaults to ``entity``. Rows are sorted by sample, entity, position.
    """
    columns: dict[str, list] = {name: [] for name in SS2_SCHEMA}
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split(None, 5)
        position = _to_int(fields[0])
        if position is None:
            continue
        fields += [None] * (6 - len(fields))
        residue, ss_code = fields[1], fields[2]
        p_coil, p_helix, p_strand = (_to_float(f) for f in fields[3:6])
        if ss_code == "H":
            value = p_helix
        elif ss_code == "E":
            value = p_strand
        else:
            value = p_coil
        columns["entity"].append(entity)
        columns["sample"].append(sample if sample is not None else entity)
        columns["position"].append(position)
        columns["residue"].append(residue)
        columns["ss_code"].append(ss_code)
        columns["category"].append(STATES.get(ss_code) if ss_code is not None else None)
        columns["value"].append(value)
        columns["p_coil"].append(p_coil)
        columns["p_helix"].append(p_helix)
        columns["p_strand"].append(p_strand)
    return pl.DataFrame(columns, schema=SS2_SCHEMA).sort(["sample", "entity", "position"])


def segments(states: Sequence[str]) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """Runs of identical states as ``(state, start, end)``, 1-based and inclusive.

    ``segments("CCHHHE")`` -> ``[("C", 1, 2), ("H", 3, 5), ("E", 6, 6)]``.
    """
    runs: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
    for index, state in enumerate(states, start=1):
        if runs and runs[-1][0] == state:
            runs[-1] = (state, runs[-1][1], index)
        else:
            runs.append((state, index, index))
    return runs
files.depictio/recipes/lib/stable_expression.p:
"""Shared parsing for nf-core/stableexpression outputs.

stableexpression downloads public expression datasets (Expression Atlas, GEO) for
one species, maps their gene ids to Ensembl, filters out samples with too many
zeros or missing values, normalises every dataset (TPM / CPM, then a quantile
normalisation to a uniform distribution, so every value lies in 0 to 1), merges
them into one gene by sample matrix and scores the most stable genes of each
expression section. The tables it publishes, and what this module reads from
them:

* ``reporting/all_genes_summary.csv``: one row per gene of the merged matrix,
  with its expression statistics (overall and per platform), its expression
  section (``section_1`` holds the most expressed genes), and, for the
  ``nb_candidates_per_section`` candidates of each section, the four stability
  measures (Normfinder, geNorm M, coefficient of variation and its robust,
  MAD-based form), their 0-1 normalised forms, the stability score (lower is
  more stable) and the rank within the section. Non-candidates carry a rank
  past the candidates that orders nothing, so it is dropped here.
* ``merged_data/all_counts.parquet`` (and ``all_counts.imputed.parquet``): the
  merged matrix, ``gene_id`` then one Float32 column per sample.
* ``merged_data/whole_design.csv``: ``batch`` (the dataset), ``condition`` (a
  group local to its dataset, ``g1``, ``g2`` ...) and ``sample``.
* ``datasets/<platform>/<normalisation>/<dataset>/<dataset>.design.csv``: the
  same design per downloaded dataset, before any filter. The directory is the
  only place a dataset's platform and normalisation state are written.
* ``statistics/``: per-dataset ID mapping counts, the samples each filter kept
  and rejected, and three ragged tables (``ratio_zeros.csv``,
  ``ratio_nulls.csv``, ``skewness.csv``: a dataset id, then one value per
  sample, no header).
* ``errors/renaming_failure_reasons.tsv`` and ``warnings/renaming_warning_reasons.tsv``:
  why a dataset's gene ids could not be mapped, or how many were.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

from depictio.models.models.transforms import RecipeSource

#: Platform directory names under ``datasets/`` and how the dashboard prints them.
PLATFORM_LABELS: dict[str, str] = {"microarray": "Microarray", "rnaseq": "RNA-seq"}
#: Normalisation-state directory names (the data as published by the database).
NORMALISATION_LABELS: dict[str, str] = {"normalised": "Normalised", "raw": "Raw counts"}

#: The pipeline's five expression levels, most expressed first.
EXPRESSION_LEVELS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "Very high expression",
    "High expression",
    "Medium range",
    "Low expression",
    "Very low expression",
)

#: Read any CSV as raw lines: one text column per line (the ragged statistics
#: tables have no header and a different width on every row).
LINE_READ_KWARGS: dict = {
    "separator": "\x1f",
    "has_header": False,
    "quote_char": None,
    "infer_schema_length": 0,
}
LINE_COLUMN = "column_1"

#: Read every column as text; the recipes cast what they use.
TEXT_READ_KWARGS: dict = {"infer_schema_length": 0}

_DATASET_PATH_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|/)datasets/(?P<platform>[^/]+)/(?P<normalisation>[^/]+)/(?P<dataset>[^/]+)/"
)
_ATLAS_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<accession>E_[A-Z]+_\d+)(?:_(?P<array>A_[A-Z0-9]+_\d+))?(?:_.*)?$")
_SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"(\d+)\s*$")

# The four stability measures of all_genes_summary.csv, in the pipeline's
# order (its --stability_score_weights order), with the names used here.
# Each entry: the pipeline's column, its name here, the stem of its normalised
# form and score part (``<stem>_norm``, ``<stem>_part``), and its label.
STABILITY_MEASURES: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, str], ...] = (
    ("normfinder_stability_value", "normfinder_stability", "normfinder", "Normfinder"),
    ("genorm_m_measure", "genorm_m", "genorm", "geNorm M"),
    ("coefficient_of_variation", "cv", "cv", "Coefficient of variation"),
    ("robust_coefficient_of_variation_median", "robust_cv", "robust_cv", "Robust CV"),
)
MISSING_COMPONENT = "Missing values"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Datasets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def platform_label(name: str | None) -> str | None:
    """``rnaseq`` -> ``RNA-seq``; an unknown platform keeps its name."""
    if name is None:
        return None
    return PLATFORM_LABELS.get(name.lower(), name)


def normalisation_label(name: str | None) -> str | None:
    """``raw`` -> ``Raw counts``; an unknown state keeps its name."""
    if name is None:
        return None
    return NORMALISATION_LABELS.get(name.lower(), name)


def accession_of(dataset: str) -> str:
    """The database accession a dataset id was built from.

    Expression Atlas ids read ``E_GEOD_10070_A_AFFY_44`` (accession, then the
    array design of a microarray experiment) or ``E_MTAB_9962_rnaseq``; the
    accession is printed the way the database writes it, ``E-GEOD-10070``. Any
    other id (GEO, a user dataset) is its own accession.
    """
    match = _ATLAS_RE.match(dataset)
    if match is None:
        return dataset
    return match.group("accession").replace("_", "-")


def array_design_of(dataset: str) -> str | None:
    """``A-AFFY-44`` for an Expression Atlas microarray dataset, else None."""
    match = _ATLAS_RE.match(dataset)
    if match is None or match.group("array") is None:
        return None
    return match.group("array").replace("_", "-")


def dataset_directories(designs: pl.DataFrame, path_col: str = "source_path") -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per dataset directory: ``dataset``, ``platform``, ``normalisation``.

    ``designs`` holds the per-dataset ``*.design.csv`` files read with a
    ``source_path`` column; the platform and normalisation state are the two
    directory levels above the dataset's own directory.
    """
    parts = designs.select(
        pl.col(path_col).str.extract_groups(_DATASET_PATH_RE.pattern).alias("_m")
    ).unnest("_m")
    out = (
        parts.drop_nulls("dataset")
        .unique(subset="dataset", keep="first")
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("platform").map_elements(platform_label, return_dtype=pl.Utf8),
            pl.col("normalisation").map_elements(normalisation_label, return_dtype=pl.Utf8),
        )
    )
    return out.select("dataset", "platform", "normalisation").sort("dataset")


def guess_platform(dataset: str) -> str:
    """Platform of a dataset whose directory was not published, from its id."""
    return (
        PLATFORM_LABELS["rnaseq"] if dataset.endswith("_rnaseq") else PLATFORM_LABELS["microarray"]
    )


def ragged_medians(lines: pl.DataFrame | None, name: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """``dataset`` and the median of its per-sample values, from a ragged table.

    ``ratio_zeros.csv``, ``ratio_nulls.csv`` and ``skewness.csv`` write a dataset
    id, then one value per sample, with no header and a different number of
    fields on every row.
    """
    if lines is None or lines.is_empty():
        return pl.DataFrame(schema={"dataset": pl.Utf8, name: pl.Float64})
    rows: list[tuple[str, float | None]] = []
    for line in lines.get_column(LINE_COLUMN).to_list():
        if line is None:
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in str(line).split(",")]
        if not cells or not cells[0]:
            continue
        values = []
        for cell in cells[1:]:
            try:
                value = float(cell)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if np.isfinite(value):
                values.append(value)
        rows.append((cells[0], float(np.median(values)) if values else None))
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema={"dataset": pl.Utf8, name: pl.Float64}, orient="row").unique(
        subset="dataset", keep="last"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Genes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def section_index(section: str | None) -> int | None:
    """``section_3`` -> 3."""
    if section is None:
        return None
    match = _SECTION_RE.search(section)
    return int(match.group(1)) if match else None


def section_label(index: int | None, n_sections: int) -> str | None:
    """``Section 03`` of ten: zero-padded so the sections sort as numbers do."""
    if index is None:
        return None
    width = max(2, len(str(n_sections)))
    return f"Section {index:0{width}d}"


def _float(col: str) -> pl.Expr:
    return pl.col(col).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).fill_nan(None)


def load_gene_summary(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """``all_genes_summary.csv`` (read as text) with typed, renamed columns.

    Every gene keeps ``gene_id``; ``gene_name`` is its symbol, or its id when
    the metadata has none (a lncRNA without a name), so a label is never empty.
    ``section`` becomes ``Section 01`` ... with ``section_index``. Candidates
    keep their rank within the section as ``section_rank``; the others get null.
    The per-platform columns the pipeline writes (``rnaseq_mean``,
    ``microarray_coefficient_of_variation`` ...) are kept under short names.
    """
    needed = [
        "mean", "median", "standard_deviation", "median_absolute_deviation",
        "coefficient_of_variation", "robust_coefficient_of_variation_median",
        "ratio_nulls_in_all_samples", "ratio_nulls_in_valid_samples", "ratio_zeros",
        "expression_level_quantile_interval", "stability_score", "rank",
        *[raw for raw, _v, _s, _l in STABILITY_MEASURES],
        *[f"{raw}_normalised" for raw, _v, _s, _l in STABILITY_MEASURES],
    ]  # fmt: skip
    # A measure the run skipped (geNorm with --skip_genorm) has no column at all.
    df = raw.with_columns(
        [pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8).alias(c) for c in needed if c not in raw.columns]
    )
    sections = df.get_column("section").map_elements(section_index, return_dtype=pl.Int64)
    n_sections = int(sections.max() or 1)
    is_candidate = (
        pl.col("is_candidate").cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).fill_null(0) == 1
        if "is_candidate" in df.columns
        else _float("stability_score").is_not_null()
    )
    name = pl.col("name") if "name" in df.columns else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8)
    name = pl.when(name.is_in(["", "None", "nan", "NaN"])).then(None).otherwise(name)
    exprs: list[pl.Expr] = [
        pl.col("gene_id"),
        name.alias("gene_symbol"),
        pl.coalesce(name, pl.col("gene_id")).alias("gene_name"),
        (pl.col("description") if "description" in df.columns else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8))
        .replace({"": None, "None": None})
        .alias("description"),
        sections.alias("section_index"),
        is_candidate.alias("_candidate"),
        _float("mean").alias("mean"),
        _float("median").alias("median"),
        _float("standard_deviation").alias("standard_deviation"),
        _float("median_absolute_deviation").alias("mad"),
        _float("coefficient_of_variation").alias("cv"),
        _float("robust_coefficient_of_variation_median").alias("robust_cv"),
        (1 - _float("ratio_nulls_in_all_samples")).alias("measured_share"),
        _float("ratio_nulls_in_valid_samples").alias("missing_penalty"),
        _float("ratio_zeros").alias("zero_share"),
        _float("expression_level_quantile_interval").alias("expression_percentile"),
        (
            pl.col("expression_level_status")
            if "expression_level_status" in df.columns
            else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8)
        ).alias("expression_level"),
        _float("stability_score").alias("stability_score"),
        pl.col("rank").cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("_rank"),
        (
            pl.col("original_gene_ids").str.split(";").list.len().cast(pl.Int64)
            if "original_gene_ids" in df.columns
            else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Int64)
        ).alias("source_ids"),
    ]
    for raw_name, value_col, stem, _label in STABILITY_MEASURES:
        if value_col not in ("cv", "robust_cv"):  # both are expression statistics too, above
            exprs.append(_float(raw_name).alias(value_col))
        exprs.append(_float(f"{raw_name}_normalised").alias(f"{stem}_norm"))
    for platform in PLATFORM_LABELS:
        for stat, short in (("mean", "mean"), ("coefficient_of_variation", "cv")):
            col = f"{platform}_{stat}"
            if col in df.columns:
                exprs.append(_float(col).alias(f"{platform}_{short}"))
    out = df.select(exprs)
    out = out.with_columns(
        pl.col("section_index")
        .map_elements(lambda i: section_label(i, n_sections), return_dtype=pl.Utf8)
        .alias("section"),
        pl.when(pl.col("_candidate")).then(pl.col("_rank")).otherwise(None).alias("section_rank"),
        pl.when(pl.col("_candidate"))
        .then(pl.lit("Candidate"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("Not a candidate"))
        .alias("candidate"),
    )
    # Which platforms measured the gene, from the per-platform means.
    platform_cols = [p for p in PLATFORM_LABELS if f"{p}_mean" in out.columns]
    if platform_cols:
        present = [pl.col(f"{p}_mean").is_not_null() for p in platform_cols]
        label = pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8)
        if len(platform_cols) == 2:
            label = (
                pl.when(present[0] & present[1])
                .then(pl.lit("Both platforms"))
                .when(present[0])
                .then(pl.lit(f"{PLATFORM_LABELS[platform_cols[0]]} only"))
                .when(present[1])
                .then(pl.lit(f"{PLATFORM_LABELS[platform_cols[1]]} only"))
                .otherwise(None)
            )
        else:
            label = (
                pl.when(present[0])
                .then(pl.lit(f"{PLATFORM_LABELS[platform_cols[0]]} only"))
                .otherwise(None)
            )
        out = out.with_columns(label.alias("platforms"))
    else:
        out = out.with_columns(pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("platforms"))
    return out.drop("_rank")


def stability_weights(candidates: pl.DataFrame) -> dict[str, float]:
    """The weights of the four measures in the stability score, recovered from it.

    The pipeline scores a candidate as ``missing_penalty + sum(w_i * norm_i)``
    over the normalised measures it computed (``--stability_score_weights``,
    0.25 each by default; a measure the run skipped, geNorm with
    ``--skip_genorm``, adds nothing). The weights are a run parameter that no
    table records, so they are solved for by least squares over the candidates
    and rounded to 4 decimals. Too few candidates, or a fit that does not
    reproduce the scores, falls back to the default equal weights.
    """
    shorts = [stem for _raw, _value, stem, _label in STABILITY_MEASURES]
    default = {short: 0.25 for short in shorts}
    usable = [s for s in shorts if candidates.get_column(f"{s}_norm").is_not_null().any()]
    if not usable or candidates.height < len(usable) + 2:
        return default
    x = candidates.select([pl.col(f"{s}_norm").fill_null(0.0) for s in usable]).to_numpy()
    y = (
        candidates.get_column("stability_score")
        - candidates.get_column("missing_penalty").fill_null(0.0)
    ).to_numpy()
    keep = np.isfinite(y)
    if keep.sum() < len(usable) + 2:
        return default
    solution, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(x[keep], y[keep], rcond=None)
    if np.nanmax(np.abs(x[keep] @ solution - y[keep])) > 1e-3:
        return default
    weights = {s: 0.0 for s in shorts}
    weights.update({s: round(float(w), 4) for s, w in zip(usable, solution, strict=True)})
    return weights


def candidates_with_parts(summary: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The candidates of ``all_genes_summary.csv``, ranked, with the score split in parts."""
    genes = load_gene_summary(summary)
    candidates = genes.filter(
        (pl.col("candidate") == "Candidate") & pl.col("stability_score").is_not_null()
    )
    if candidates.is_empty():
        raise ValueError("all_genes_summary.csv holds no scored candidate gene")
    weights = stability_weights(candidates)
    return candidates.with_columns(
        overall_rank_expr(),
        pl.col("missing_penalty").fill_null(0.0),
        *[
            (pl.col(f"{stem}_norm").fill_null(0.0) * weights[stem]).alias(f"{stem}_part")
            for _raw, _value, stem, _label in STABILITY_MEASURES
        ],
    ).with_columns(
        # 1 / rank: the most stable gene in view outweighs any other, so a text
        # value's `top` aggregation (largest summed weight) names it.
        (1.0 / pl.col("overall_rank")).alias("rank_weight"),
        # Each measure's own rank within the section, 1 the steadiest: two
        # measures that agree put a gene on the diagonal of one against the other.
        *[
            pl.col(raw).rank(method="ordinal").over("section").cast(pl.Int64).alias(f"{stem}_rank")
            for raw, stem in (("normfinder_stability", "normfinder"), ("genorm_m", "genorm"))
        ],
    )


def overall_rank_expr() -> pl.Expr:
    """Rank over every candidate by stability score, 1 the most stable (ties by order)."""
    return pl.col("stability_score").rank(method="ordinal").cast(pl.Int64).alias("overall_rank")


def box_stats(values: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float | int | None]:
    """Tukey box statistics of ``values`` (NaN dropped), as a box plot draws them.

    Quartiles are linearly interpolated (numpy's default, the renderer's too);
    each whisker ends at the furthest value within 1.5 IQR of its quartile.
    """
    v = values[np.isfinite(values)]
    if v.size == 0:
        return {
            k: None for k in ("q1", "median", "q3", "lower", "upper", "mean", "sd", "min", "max")
        } | {"n": 0}
    v = np.sort(v)
    q1, median, q3 = (float(x) for x in np.quantile(v, [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]))
    iqr = q3 - q1
    low_fence, high_fence = q1 - 1.5 * iqr, q3 + 1.5 * iqr
    inside = v[(v >= low_fence) & (v <= high_fence)]
    lower = float(min(inside.min(), q1)) if inside.size else q1
    upper = float(max(inside.max(), q3)) if inside.size else q3
    return {
        "q1": q1,
        "median": median,
        "q3": q3,
        "lower": lower,
        "upper": upper,
        "mean": float(v.mean()),
        "sd": float(v.std(ddof=1)) if v.size > 1 else 0.0,
        "min": float(v[0]),
        "max": float(v[-1]),
        "n": int(v.size),
    }


def gene_rows(counts: pl.DataFrame, gene_ids: list[str]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The rows of ``gene_ids`` in a gene by sample matrix (``gene_id`` first)."""
    return counts.filter(pl.col("gene_id").is_in(gene_ids))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Datasets through the pipeline
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: The steps a downloaded dataset goes through, in order, with the column of
#: ``dataset_table`` that holds the samples still in after that step.
FUNNEL_STEPS: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    ("Downloaded", "samples_downloaded"),
    ("Gene IDs mapped", "samples_id_mapped"),
    ("Zero filter", "samples_after_zero_filter"),
    ("Missing-value filter", "samples_kept"),
)

OUTCOME_MERGED = "Merged"
OUTCOME_NO_GENE = "No gene mapped"
OUTCOME_RARE_GENES = "Only rare genes"
OUTCOME_FILTERED = "All samples filtered out"


def dataset_sources() -> list[RecipeSource]:
    """The sources ``dataset_table`` reads, shared by every dataset-level recipe.

    Only the per-dataset designs are required: every run publishes them. The
    statistics tables are written by steps a run can skip (``--skip_id_mapping``)
    and the reason tables only when a dataset failed or lost ids, so each is an
    optional single file.
    """
    tsv = {"separator": "\t", "infer_schema_length": 0}
    return [
        RecipeSource(
            ref="designs",
            glob_pattern="datasets/*/*/*/*.design.csv",
            format="csv",
            read_kwargs=TEXT_READ_KWARGS,
            source_path="source_path",
            input_schema={"batch": pl.Utf8, "condition": pl.Utf8, "sample": pl.Utf8},
        ),
        RecipeSource(
            ref="id_mapping",
            path="statistics/id_mapping_stats.csv",
            format="csv",
            read_kwargs=TEXT_READ_KWARGS,
            optional=True,
        ),
        RecipeSource(
            ref="zero_filter",
            path="statistics/zero_values_filter_stats.csv",
            format="csv",
            read_kwargs=TEXT_READ_KWARGS,
            optional=True,
        ),
        RecipeSource(
            ref="missing_filter",
            path="statistics/missing_values_filter_stats.csv",
            format="csv",
            read_kwargs=TEXT_READ_KWARGS,
            optional=True,
        ),
        RecipeSource(
            ref="failures",
            path="errors/renaming_failure_reasons.tsv",
            format="csv",
            read_kwargs=tsv,
            optional=True,
        ),
        RecipeSource(
            ref="warnings",
            path="warnings/renaming_warning_reasons.tsv",
            format="csv",
            read_kwargs=tsv,
            optional=True,
        ),
        *[
            RecipeSource(
                ref=ref,
                path=f"statistics/{ref}.csv",
                format="csv",
                read_kwargs=LINE_READ_KWARGS,
                optional=True,
            )
            for ref in ("ratio_zeros", "ratio_nulls", "skewness")
        ],
    ]


def _int_frame(df: pl.DataFrame | None, columns: dict[str, str]) -> pl.DataFrame | None:
    """``dataset`` plus ``columns`` (source -> output name) cast to Int64."""
    if df is None or df.is_empty() or "dataset" not in df.columns:
        return None
    present = {src: out for src, out in columns.items() if src in df.columns}
    return df.select(
        pl.col("dataset"),
        *[pl.col(src).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias(out) for src, out in present.items()],
    ).unique(subset="dataset", keep="last")


def _reasons(df: pl.DataFrame | None, name: str) -> pl.DataFrame | None:
    """``dataset`` and the reason text of an errors/ or warnings/ table."""
    if df is None or df.is_empty():
        return None
    cols = {c.lower(): c for c in df.columns}
    if "dataset" not in cols or "reason" not in cols:
        return None
    return (
        df.select(pl.col(cols["dataset"]).alias("dataset"), pl.col(cols["reason"]).alias(name))
        .group_by("dataset", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(pl.col(name).str.join(" | "))
    )


def _ensure(df: pl.DataFrame, columns: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """``df`` with every column of ``columns`` it lacks added as nulls."""
    return df.with_columns(
        [
            pl.lit(None, dtype=dtype).alias(col)
            for col, dtype in columns.items()
            if col not in df.columns
        ]
    )


def dataset_table(sources: dict[str, pl.DataFrame | None]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per downloaded dataset, with what each step of the pipeline did to it.

    Sources (all but ``designs`` optional): ``designs`` (every
    ``datasets/*/*/*/*.design.csv`` with ``source_path``), ``id_mapping``,
    ``zero_filter``, ``missing_filter`` (the ``statistics/`` tables),
    ``failures`` / ``warnings`` (the renaming reasons) and the ragged
    ``ratio_zeros`` / ``ratio_nulls`` / ``skewness`` tables read as lines.

    A step the dataset never reached holds 0 samples, so a funnel sums
    cleanly; a run without ID mapping (``--skip_id_mapping``) counts every
    dataset as mapped.
    """
    designs = sources["designs"]
    dirs = dataset_directories(designs)
    downloaded = (
        designs.filter(pl.col("batch").is_not_null())
        .group_by(pl.col("batch").alias("dataset"))
        .agg(
            pl.col("sample").n_unique().cast(pl.Int64).alias("samples_downloaded"),
            pl.col("condition").n_unique().cast(pl.Int64).alias("conditions"),
        )
    )
    out = dirs.join(downloaded, on="dataset", how="left")

    id_stats = _int_frame(
        sources.get("id_mapping"),
        {
            "final": "genes_kept",
            "merged": "ids_merged",
            "not_valid": "genes_rare",
            "unmapped": "ids_unmapped",
        },
    )
    zero = _int_frame(
        sources.get("zero_filter"),
        {"kept": "samples_after_zero_filter", "rejected": "samples_rejected_zeros"},
    )
    missing = _int_frame(
        sources.get("missing_filter"),
        {"kept": "samples_kept", "rejected": "samples_rejected_missing"},
    )
    for frame in (id_stats, zero, missing):
        if frame is not None:
            out = out.join(frame, on="dataset", how="left")
    for ref, name in (("failures", "failure_reason"), ("warnings", "mapping_note")):
        reasons = _reasons(sources.get(ref), name)
        if reasons is not None:
            out = out.join(reasons, on="dataset", how="left")
    for ref, name in (
        ("ratio_zeros", "zero_share"),
        ("ratio_nulls", "missing_share"),
        ("skewness", "skewness"),
    ):
        out = out.join(ragged_medians(sources.get(ref), name), on="dataset", how="left")
    out = _ensure(
        out,
        {
            "genes_kept": pl.Int64,
            "ids_merged": pl.Int64,
            "genes_rare": pl.Int64,
            "ids_unmapped": pl.Int64,
            "samples_after_zero_filter": pl.Int64,
            "samples_rejected_zeros": pl.Int64,
            "samples_kept": pl.Int64,
            "samples_rejected_missing": pl.Int64,
            "failure_reason": pl.Utf8,
            "mapping_note": pl.Utf8,
        },
    )

    # Every id the dataset came with is kept, merged into another id (which
    # counts the rare genes too: ``merged`` is mapped minus kept) or unmapped.
    # A dataset that lost every gene as rare writes 0 merged, not the rare count.
    mapped = pl.col("genes_kept") + pl.max_horizontal("ids_merged", "genes_rare")
    original = mapped + pl.col("ids_unmapped")
    has_stats = pl.col("genes_kept").is_not_null()
    failed = pl.col("failure_reason").is_not_null() | (has_stats & (pl.col("genes_kept") == 0))
    out = out.with_columns(
        pl.col("dataset").map_elements(accession_of, return_dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("accession"),
        pl.col("dataset").map_elements(array_design_of, return_dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("array_design"),
        original.alias("gene_ids_in"),
        pl.when(has_stats & (original > 0))
        .then((mapped / original).round(4))
        .otherwise(None)
        .alias("mapped_share"),
        (pl.col("ids_merged") - pl.col("genes_rare")).clip(lower_bound=0).alias("ids_collapsed"),
        pl.when(failed).then(0).otherwise(1).cast(pl.Int64).alias("id_mapped"),
        pl.col("samples_after_zero_filter").fill_null(0),
        pl.col("samples_kept").fill_null(0),
        pl.col("samples_rejected_zeros").fill_null(0),
        pl.col("samples_rejected_missing").fill_null(0),
    )
    out = out.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("id_mapped") == 1)
        .then(pl.col("samples_downloaded"))
        .otherwise(0)
        .alias("samples_id_mapped"),
        pl.when(pl.col("id_mapped") == 0)
        .then(
            pl.when(pl.col("failure_reason").str.contains("(?i)rare"))
            .then(pl.lit(OUTCOME_RARE_GENES))
            .otherwise(pl.lit(OUTCOME_NO_GENE))
        )
        .when(pl.col("samples_kept") == 0)
        .then(pl.lit(OUTCOME_FILTERED))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(OUTCOME_MERGED))
        .alias("outcome"),
        pl.lit(1, dtype=pl.Int64).alias("downloaded"),
        (pl.col("samples_kept") > 0).cast(pl.Int64).alias("merged"),
        pl.when(pl.col("samples_downloaded") > 0)
        .then((pl.col("samples_kept") / pl.col("samples_downloaded")).round(4))
        .otherwise(None)
        .alias("kept_share"),
    )
    return out.sort("platform", "dataset")
files.depictio/recipes/lib/star_logs.py:
"""Read STAR's ``Log.final.out`` and ``SJ.out.tab`` with Polars alone.

Every STAR-based nf-core pipeline (rnaseq, rnavar, rnafusion, rnasplice,
circrna, ...) publishes the aligner's own two per-sample summaries next to the
BAM: ``<sample>.Log.final.out`` (the read fate, the splice and the error
rates) and ``<sample>.SJ.out.tab`` (one row per collapsed splice junction).
MultiQC parses the first into a few percentages and never reads the second, so
the catalog reads both itself. Shared here because three catalog recipes
(``star/log_final``, ``star/read_fate``, ``star/junctions``) need the same
parsing, and recipes may not import each other.

``Log.final.out`` is a two-column key/value list, ``<key> |<TAB><value>``, with
section titles (``UNIQUE READS:``) that carry no value. A source therefore reads
one LINE per row (a separator the file cannot contain), and the key is
everything before the last ``|``.

The sample is the file name with STAR's suffix removed: ``GM12878_REP1.Log.final.out``
and ``GM12878_REP1.SJ.out.tab`` both name ``GM12878_REP1``. nf-core writes the
prefix as the samplesheet id, so nothing else needs stripping.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import polars as pl

#: Column holding one full report line (sources read with a separator the
#: report cannot contain).
RAW_LINE_COL = "raw_line"
#: Column carrying the report's path (``source_path`` on the recipe source).
SOURCE_PATH_COL = "source_path"

_STAR_SUFFIX_RE = r"\.(?:Log\.final\.out|SJ\.out\.tab)(?:\.gz)?$"

#: ``Log.final.out`` key (stripped) -> output column. Percent keys keep their
#: number and lose the ``%`` sign; counts are integers.
LOG_KEYS: dict[str, str] = {
    "Number of input reads": "input_reads",
    "Average input read length": "avg_input_read_length",
    "Uniquely mapped reads number": "uniquely_mapped",
    "Uniquely mapped reads %": "uniquely_mapped_pct",
    "Average mapped length": "avg_mapped_length",
    "Number of splices: Total": "splices_total",
    "Number of splices: Annotated (sjdb)": "splices_annotated",
    "Number of splices: GT/AG": "splices_gt_ag",
    "Number of splices: GC/AG": "splices_gc_ag",
    "Number of splices: AT/AC": "splices_at_ac",
    "Number of splices: Non-canonical": "splices_noncanonical",
    "Mismatch rate per base, %": "mismatch_rate_pct",
    "Deletion rate per base": "deletion_rate_pct",
    "Insertion rate per base": "insertion_rate_pct",
    "Number of reads mapped to multiple loci": "multimapped",
    "% of reads mapped to multiple loci": "multimapped_pct",
    "Number of reads mapped to too many loci": "too_many_loci",
    "% of reads mapped to too many loci": "too_many_loci_pct",
    "Number of reads unmapped: too many mismatches": "unmapped_mismatches",
    "% of reads unmapped: too many mismatches": "unmapped_mismatches_pct",
    "Number of reads unmapped: too short": "unmapped_too_short",
    "% of reads unmapped: too short": "unmapped_too_short_pct",
    "Number of reads unmapped: other": "unmapped_other",
    "% of reads unmapped: other": "unmapped_other_pct",
    "Number of chimeric reads": "chimeric",
    "% of chimeric reads": "chimeric_pct",
}

#: Columns read as integers; every other ``LOG_KEYS`` column is a float.
INT_COLUMNS = frozenset(
    {
        "input_reads",
        "uniquely_mapped",
        "splices_total",
        "splices_annotated",
        "splices_gt_ag",
        "splices_gc_ag",
        "splices_at_ac",
        "splices_noncanonical",
        "multimapped",
        "too_many_loci",
        "unmapped_mismatches",
        "unmapped_too_short",
        "unmapped_other",
        "chimeric",
    }
)

#: SJ.out.tab column 5, the intron motif STAR assigns from the genome.
#: Odd codes are the + strand reading, even ones the - strand reading of the
#: same motif, so they fold onto four classes.
MOTIF_CLASSES: dict[int, str] = {
    0: "non-canonical",
    1: "GT/AG",
    2: "GT/AG",
