    3: "GC/AG",
    4: "GC/AG",
    5: "AT/AC",
    6: "AT/AC",
}
#: SJ.out.tab has no header; these are STAR's documented column meanings.
SJ_COLUMNS = [
    "chrom",
    "intron_start",
    "intron_end",
    "strand",
    "motif",
    "annotated",
    "unique_reads",
    "multimapping_reads",
    "max_overhang",
]


def sample_from_path(path: str) -> str:
    """``reports/star/GM12878_REP1/GM12878_REP1.Log.final.out`` -> ``GM12878_REP1``."""
    name = str(path).replace("\\", "/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return re.sub(_STAR_SUFFIX_RE, "", name)


def _number(text: str) -> float | None:
    cleaned = text.strip().rstrip("%").strip()
    try:
        return float(cleaned)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def parse_log_final(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per ``Log.final.out``: ``sample`` plus every ``LOG_KEYS`` column.

    A key a STAR version does not write comes back null rather than failing the
    collection; two reports of one sample keep the first.
    """
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for (path,), block in raw.group_by(SOURCE_PATH_COL, maintain_order=True):
        row: dict[str, object] = {"sample": sample_from_path(str(path))}
        for line in block[RAW_LINE_COL].to_list():
            text = str(line or "")
            if "|" not in text:
                continue
            key, _, value = text.rpartition("|")
            column = LOG_KEYS.get(key.strip())
            if column is None:
                continue
            number = _number(value)
            row[column] = int(number) if number is not None and column in INT_COLUMNS else number
        rows.append(row)
    schema: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {"sample": pl.Utf8}
    schema.update({c: pl.Int64 if c in INT_COLUMNS else pl.Float64 for c in LOG_KEYS.values()})
    if not rows:
        return pl.DataFrame(schema=schema)
    frame = pl.DataFrame(rows, infer_schema_length=None)
    for column, dtype in schema.items():
        if column not in frame.columns:
            frame = frame.with_columns(pl.lit(None, dtype=dtype).alias(column))
    return (
        frame.select([pl.col(c).cast(t) for c, t in schema.items()])
        .unique(subset="sample", keep="first", maintain_order=True)
        .sort("sample")
    )
files.depictio/recipes/lib/strand_coverage.py:
"""Strand-specific coverage bedGraphs, binned into genomic windows.

Nascent-transcription pipelines (nf-core/nascent: GRO-seq, PRO-seq and their
relatives) publish one coverage bedGraph per library and strand, written by
``bedtools genomecov -bg -strand +`` and ``-strand -``:

    coverage_graphs/<sample>.plus.bedGraph
    coverage_graphs/<sample>.minus.bedGraph

Four columns, no header: contig, start, end, read depth over that interval.
A human library holds 4 to 10 million intervals per strand (100 to 450 MB), so
nothing here reads a file whole. Each file streams through
``depictio/recipes/lib/genomic_bins.py``, whose lazy ``group_by`` keeps one batch
in memory at a time.

What a window holds is **read bases**: depth times interval width, summed over
the intervals that start in the window. Averaging the depth column itself (what
``bin_coordinate_frame`` does with a plain value) would weigh a 1 bp interval
like a 5 kb one; the product is the quantity a coverage track integrates, and it
divides into a per-million share of the library without any read-length
assumption. An interval that straddles a window edge is counted in the window
its start falls in, which at 100 kb and wider moves a negligible share.

Shared by the bedtools catalog recipes (``bedtools/strand_bins.py``
and ``bedtools/strand_summary.py``) because recipes may not import one
another.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl

from depictio.recipes.lib.genomic_bins import bin_coordinate_frame

#: ``<sample>.plus.bedGraph`` / ``<sample>.minus.bedGraph``, gzipped or not.
#: The ``dreg`` bedGraph nf-core/nascent writes beside them (a signed 3' end
#: count for dREG) does not match and is never read as coverage.
STRAND_BEDGRAPH_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<sample>.+)\.(?P<strand>plus|minus)\.bedGraph(?:\.gz)?$")
#: Column names of a bedtools bedGraph, which ships no header line.
BEDGRAPH_COLUMNS = ["chrom", "start", "end", "depth"]
#: Column of the index scan that carries each file's path.
SOURCE_PATH_COL = "source_path"
#: Window width of every binned panel. 250 kb leaves about 12,000 windows on a
#: mammalian genome: fine enough to separate loci a megabase apart, coarse
#: enough for one lane per library to draw genome-wide from a table.
WINDOW_SIZE = 250_000
#: A contig with fewer windows than this is assembly debris (unplaced and alt
#: scaffolds, the mitochondrion, a viral episome): its signal still counts in the
#: library total, but it gets no window of its own.
MIN_WINDOWS_PER_CONTIG = 20
#: Mitochondrial contig names across UCSC, Ensembl and GenBank-style references.
MITO_RE = r"^(?:chr)?(?:M|MT|Mito|mitochondrion)$"


def strand_bedgraph_files(paths: Iterable[str]) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """``(path, sample, strand)`` for each strand bedGraph among ``paths``, sorted.

    Paths that are not a plus or minus bedGraph (the dREG bedGraph, anything
    else a recursive scan picked up) are skipped.
    """
    out: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    for path in sorted({str(p) for p in paths if p}):
        match = STRAND_BEDGRAPH_RE.match(Path(path).name)
        if match:
            out.append((path, match.group("sample"), match.group("strand")))
    return out


def files_from_index(index: pl.DataFrame | None, label: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """The strand bedGraphs a one-row-per-file index scan points at.

    Raises ``ValueError`` (prefixed with ``label``) when the index is empty,
    lacks the path column or names no strand bedGraph.
    """
    if index is None or index.is_empty():
        raise ValueError(f"{label}: the bedGraph index is empty")
    if SOURCE_PATH_COL not in index.columns:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label}: the bedGraph index must be scanned with include_file_paths={SOURCE_PATH_COL}"
        )
    files = strand_bedgraph_files(index.get_column(SOURCE_PATH_COL).to_list())
    if not files:
        raise ValueError(f"{label}: no <sample>.plus/.minus.bedGraph among the indexed files")
    return files


def scan_bedgraph(path: str) -> pl.LazyFrame:
    """Lazy scan of one bedGraph with a ``read_bases`` column (depth x width)."""
    frame = pl.scan_csv(
        path,
        separator="\t",
        has_header=False,
        new_columns=BEDGRAPH_COLUMNS,
        schema_overrides={
            "chrom": pl.Utf8,
            "start": pl.Int64,
            "end": pl.Int64,
            "depth": pl.Float64,
        },
        comment_prefix="track",
    )
    return frame.with_columns(
        (pl.col("depth") * (pl.col("end") - pl.col("start"))).alias("read_bases")
    )


def contig_totals(path: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Per-contig read bases, covered bases and maximum depth of one bedGraph."""
    return (
        scan_bedgraph(path)
        .group_by("chrom")
        .agg(
            pl.col("read_bases").sum().alias("read_bases"),
            (pl.col("end") - pl.col("start")).sum().alias("covered_bases"),
            pl.col("depth").max().alias("max_depth"),
        )
        .collect(engine="streaming")
    )


def bin_bedgraph(path: str, bin_size: int = WINDOW_SIZE) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Read bases per ``bin_size`` window of one bedGraph.

    Columns: ``chrom, start, end, read_bases, n`` (``n`` the intervals that
    started in the window). Windows with no interval are absent.
    """
    binned = bin_coordinate_frame(
        scan_bedgraph(path),
        chrom_col="chrom",
        pos_col="start",
        value_col="read_bases",
        bin_size=bin_size,
    )
    return binned.with_columns((pl.col("mean") * pl.col("n")).alias("read_bases")).drop("mean")


def main_contigs(windows: pl.DataFrame, min_windows: int = MIN_WINDOWS_PER_CONTIG) -> list[str]:
    """Contigs holding at least ``min_windows`` windows with signal, in any library."""
    return (
        windows.select("chrom", "start")
        .unique()
        .group_by("chrom")
        .agg(pl.len().alias("_windows"))
        .filter(pl.col("_windows") >= min_windows)
        .get_column("chrom")
        .to_list()
    )


def contig_order_expr(column: str = "chromosome") -> pl.Expr:
    """Sort key putting chr1..chr22 (or 1..22) first, in number order."""
    return (
        pl.col(column)
        .str.extract(r"^(?:chr)?(\d+)$", 1)
        .cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
        .alias("_contig_number")
    )


#: Windows kept for a comparison across libraries: those whose mean signal is at
#: least the median window's (the transcribed half of the genome) ...
TRANSCRIBED_QUANTILE = 0.5
#: ... and below this quantile, which drops the hotspot windows (ribosomal DNA
#: arrays, a few very highly transcribed loci) whose share moves with how well
#: a library was depleted rather than with transcription.
HOTSPOT_QUANTILE = 0.995


def window_id_expr() -> pl.Expr:
    """``chr1:250000-500000``, the stable name of one window."""
    return pl.concat_str(
        [
            pl.col("chromosome"),
            pl.lit(":"),
            pl.col("start").cast(pl.Utf8),
            pl.lit("-"),
            pl.col("end").cast(pl.Utf8),
        ]
    ).alias("window_id")


def comparable_windows(bins: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """``window_id, chromosome, start, end, position, mean_rpm`` of the windows to compare.

    ``bins`` is the window table of ``bedtools/strand_bins.py``. A window is
    kept when its mean ``signal_rpm`` over the libraries lies between the
    ``TRANSCRIBED_QUANTILE`` and ``HOTSPOT_QUANTILE`` of all window means.
    """
    means = (
        bins.with_columns(window_id_expr())
        .group_by("window_id", "chromosome", "start", "end", "position")
        .agg(pl.col("signal_rpm").mean().alias("mean_rpm"))
    )
    low = means.get_column("mean_rpm").quantile(TRANSCRIBED_QUANTILE)
    high = means.get_column("mean_rpm").quantile(HOTSPOT_QUANTILE)
    if low is None or high is None:
        raise ValueError("strand_coverage: no window to compare")
    return means.filter(
        (pl.col("mean_rpm") >= low) & (pl.col("mean_rpm") <= high) & (pl.col("mean_rpm") > 0)
    )
files.depictio/recipes/lib/time_course.py:
"""Time points of a time-course run: hours, order, baseline and phase.

A time course carries its design in one numeric column (hours since the first
sample) and, usually, a label (``30min``, ``2h``). Every panel downstream needs
the same four things out of it, spelled the same way:

* ``time_h``: hours, the x of every trajectory;
* ``time_order``: the rank of the time point, 1 for the earliest;
* ``time_axis``: ``log2(1 + time_h)``, the axis a time course sampled densely
  at the start (minutes) and sparsely at the end (days) reads on, so the early
  points are not crowded into the first few pixels;
* ``phase``: ``Early``, ``Mid`` or ``Late``, the tertile of the time point's
  rank among the points after the baseline, so a response can be described by
  when it peaks without naming hours a run may not have sampled.

The baseline is the earliest time point; every fold change is against it.

The design table is the source of truth (its ``time_col``, hours). A run started
without one still gets a time course when its sample ids end in a duration
(``<anything>_30min``, ``<anything>_2h``, ``_1d``): :func:`parse_hours` reads
that suffix, and only that suffix. A sample with neither is left without a
time and drops out of the trajectories rather than being placed anywhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re

import polars as pl

#: Trailing duration of a sample id or a time label: ``30min``, ``2h``, ``1.5 hr``,
#: ``3d``, ``45s``. Anchored at the end, after an underscore, dash, dot or
#: nothing, so ``GM_12h`` reads 12 and ``REP12`` reads nothing.
_DURATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[_\-.\s])(?P<value>\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?P<unit>s|sec|secs|m|min|mins|minutes?|h|hr|hrs|hours?|d|days?)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_UNIT_HOURS = {"s": 1 / 3600, "m": 1 / 60, "h": 1.0, "d": 24.0}
#: Phase labels, earliest first.
PHASES = ("Early", "Mid", "Late")
#: Phase of the baseline time point itself.
BASELINE_PHASE = "Baseline"


def parse_hours(label: str | None) -> float | None:
    """Hours encoded in the trailing duration of ``label``, else ``None``."""
    if label is None:
        return None
    match = _DURATION_RE.search(str(label).strip())
    if not match:
        return None
    unit = match.group("unit").lower()
    key = "m" if unit.startswith("m") else unit[0]
    return float(match.group("value")) * _UNIT_HOURS[key]


def format_hours(hours: float | None) -> str | None:
    """A compact label for ``hours``: ``30min``, ``2h``, ``1.5h``."""
    if hours is None or math.isnan(hours):
        return None
    if 0 < hours < 1:
        return f"{hours * 60:g}min"
    return f"{hours:g}h"


def time_columns(frame: pl.DataFrame, hours_col: str = "time_h") -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add ``time_order``, ``time_axis`` and ``phase`` from ``hours_col``.

    ``frame`` holds one row per sample (several samples may share a time
    point). Rows without hours get null in all three.
    """
    hours = pl.col(hours_col)
    points = (
        frame.select(pl.col(hours_col).cast(pl.Float64))
        .drop_nulls()
        .unique()
        .sort(hours_col)
        .get_column(hours_col)
        .to_list()
    )
    order = {h: i + 1 for i, h in enumerate(points)}
    after = points[1:]
    phase: dict[float, str] = {}
    if points:
        phase[points[0]] = BASELINE_PHASE
    for i, h in enumerate(after):
        phase[h] = PHASES[min(len(PHASES) - 1, (i * len(PHASES)) // max(1, len(after)))]
    return frame.with_columns(
        hours.cast(pl.Float64).alias(hours_col),
        hours.cast(pl.Float64)
        .replace_strict(order, default=None, return_dtype=pl.Int64)
        .alias("time_order"),
        (hours.cast(pl.Float64) + 1.0).log(2).alias("time_axis"),
        hours.cast(pl.Float64)
        .replace_strict(phase, default=None, return_dtype=pl.Utf8)
        .alias("phase"),
    )


def sample_times(
    samples: list[str],
    design: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    time_col: str | None = "time_h",
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per sample: ``sample, time_point, time_h`` and the derived columns.

    ``design`` is keyed by ``sample``. Its ``time_col`` (hours) wins over the
    duration parsed from the sample id; its ``time_point`` label is kept when it
    has one, else the label is written from the hours.
    """
    ids = sorted({str(s) for s in samples if s is not None})
    base = pl.DataFrame(
        {"sample": ids, "_parsed": [parse_hours(s) for s in ids]},
        schema={"sample": pl.Utf8, "_parsed": pl.Float64},
    )
    design_hours = pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Float64)
    design_label = pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8)
    if design is not None and not design.is_empty() and "sample" in design.columns:
        keep = {"sample": "sample"}
        if time_col and time_col != "sample" and time_col in design.columns:
            keep[time_col] = "_design_h"
        if "time_point" in design.columns:
            keep["time_point"] = "_design_label"
        picked = (
            design.select([pl.col(c).alias(a) for c, a in keep.items()])
            .with_columns(pl.col("sample").cast(pl.Utf8).str.strip_chars())
            .unique(subset="sample", keep="first")
        )
        base = base.join(picked, on="sample", how="left")
        if "_design_h" in base.columns:
            design_hours = pl.col("_design_h").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
        if "_design_label" in base.columns:
            design_label = pl.col("_design_label").cast(pl.Utf8)
    base = base.with_columns(
        pl.coalesce(design_hours, pl.col("_parsed")).alias("time_h"),
        design_label.alias("_label"),
    )
    labels = [
        label or format_hours(hours) or sample
        for sample, hours, label in zip(base["sample"], base["time_h"], base["_label"], strict=True)
    ]
    out = base.select("sample", "time_h").with_columns(
        pl.Series("time_point", labels, dtype=pl.Utf8)
    )
    return time_columns(out.select("sample", "time_point", "time_h"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Changes over time: one rule for genes and for genomic windows
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: log2 fold change against the baseline a time point needs to count as changed.
MIN_LOG2FC = 1.0
#: Changed time points (same direction) a feature needs to be called responsive.
#: A time course of nascent transcription is rarely replicated per time point, so
#: one time point alone is not evidence; two in the same direction are.
MIN_CHANGED_POINTS = 2
#: Direction labels.
UP, DOWN, FLAT = "Up", "Down", "Stable"

#: Columns of :func:`time_point_values`, besides the feature key.
TIME_POINT_COLUMNS = ("time_point", "time_h", "time_order", "time_axis", "phase")


def time_point_values(
    long: pl.DataFrame, times: pl.DataFrame, *, key: str, value_col: str
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Mean ``value_col`` per feature and time point, with its log2 fold change.

    ``long`` is one row per feature and sample; ``times`` the hub's per-sample
    time columns (``sample, time_point, time_h, time_order, time_axis, phase``).
    Samples without a time drop out. Libraries sharing a time point (replicates)
    are averaged. ``log2fc`` is the value minus the feature's value at the
    baseline (``time_order == 1``), so ``value_col`` must already be on a log2
    scale.
    """
    timed = long.join(times.filter(pl.col("time_order").is_not_null()), on="sample", how="inner")
    if timed.is_empty():
        raise ValueError("time_course: no sample has a time point")
    per_point = timed.group_by([key, *TIME_POINT_COLUMNS]).agg(
        pl.col(value_col).mean().alias("value")
    )
    baseline = per_point.filter(pl.col("time_order") == 1).select(
        key, pl.col("value").alias("baseline")
    )
    return (
        per_point.join(baseline, on=key, how="left")
        .with_columns((pl.col("value") - pl.col("baseline")).alias("log2fc"))
        .sort([key, "time_order"])
    )


def classify_changes(
    points: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    key: str,
    min_log2fc: float = MIN_LOG2FC,
    min_points: int = MIN_CHANGED_POINTS,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per feature: its peak change, when it peaks and its direction.

    ``points`` is :func:`time_point_values`. The peak is the time point after
    the baseline with the largest absolute fold change. ``direction`` is ``Up``
    or ``Down`` when the peak reaches ``min_log2fc`` and at least ``min_points``
    time points change by that much in the peak's direction (all of them on a
    run with fewer later time points), else ``Stable``.

    Columns: ``key, baseline, mean_value, dynamic_range, peak_log2fc,
    abs_peak_log2fc, peak_time_point, peak_time_h, peak_phase, last_log2fc,
    n_changed, direction``.
    """
    after = points.filter(pl.col("time_order") > 1)
    if after.is_empty():
        raise ValueError("time_course: a time course needs a time point after the baseline")
    # A run with fewer later time points than ``min_points`` asks for all of them.
    needed = min(min_points, after.get_column("time_order").n_unique())
    peak = (
        after.sort([key, pl.col("log2fc").abs()], descending=[False, True])
        .group_by(key, maintain_order=True)
        .first()
        .select(
            key,
            pl.col("log2fc").alias("peak_log2fc"),
            pl.col("time_point").alias("peak_time_point"),
            pl.col("time_h").alias("peak_time_h"),
            pl.col("phase").alias("peak_phase"),
        )
    )
    last = (
        after.sort([key, "time_order"])
        .group_by(key, maintain_order=True)
        .last()
        .select(key, pl.col("log2fc").alias("last_log2fc"))
    )
    spread = points.group_by(key).agg(
        pl.col("baseline").first(),
        pl.col("value").mean().alias("mean_value"),
        (pl.col("value").max() - pl.col("value").min()).alias("dynamic_range"),
    )
    joined = peak.join(after.select(key, "log2fc"), on=key).with_columns(
        (
            (pl.col("log2fc") * pl.col("peak_log2fc").sign() >= min_log2fc)
            & (pl.col("peak_log2fc").abs() >= min_log2fc)
        ).alias("_changed")
    )
    changed = joined.group_by(key).agg(pl.col("_changed").sum().cast(pl.Int64).alias("n_changed"))
    return (
        spread.join(peak, on=key)
        .join(last, on=key)
        .join(changed, on=key)
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("peak_log2fc").abs().alias("abs_peak_log2fc"),
            pl.when(pl.col("n_changed") >= needed)
            .then(pl.when(pl.col("peak_log2fc") > 0).then(pl.lit(UP)).otherwise(pl.lit(DOWN)))
            .otherwise(pl.lit(FLAT))
            .alias("direction"),
        )
        .sort(key)
    )


def spread_by_class(points: pl.DataFrame, *, class_col: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Median and quartiles of ``log2fc`` per class and time point.

    The shape a ``profile`` tile draws as one curve per class with its
    interquartile band: ``class_col, time_point, time_h, time_order, time_axis,
    phase, median_log2fc, q1_log2fc, q3_log2fc, n_features``.
    """
    return (
        points.group_by([class_col, *TIME_POINT_COLUMNS])
        .agg(
            pl.col("log2fc").median().alias("median_log2fc"),
            pl.col("log2fc").quantile(0.25, interpolation="linear").alias("q1_log2fc"),
            pl.col("log2fc").quantile(0.75, interpolation="linear").alias("q3_log2fc"),
            pl.len().cast(pl.Int64).alias("n_features"),
        )
        .sort([class_col, "time_order"])
    )
files.depictio/recipes/lib/vcf_somatic.py:
"""Read the VCFs of a tumour/normal pair, or of a tumour on its own, with Polars alone.

``depictio.recipes.lib.vcf.vcf_to_long`` reads a germline VCF: one sample column, a
genotype, an allele fraction. A somatic VCF is different in the one way that matters: its
genotype columns are a *pair* (normal and tumour), the callers do not agree on which comes
first, and each writes its allele evidence under its own FORMAT keys. This module reads the
callers sarek runs on a pair, one parser each:

``mutect2`` (``<tumour>_vs_<normal>.mutect2.filtered.vcf.gz``)
    FORMAT ``GT:AD:AF:DP...`` on each of two samples. Which column is the tumour is written
    in the header (``##tumor_sample=`` / ``##normal_sample=``), so the header lines must be
    in the frame; without them the normal is taken as the first column. Allele fraction is
    ``AF``, else ``AD[1] / (AD[0] + AD[1])``. The unfiltered ``.mutect2.vcf.gz`` is left out,
    its calls are the filtered file's before ``FilterMutectCalls``.
``strelka`` (``<pair>.strelka.somatic_snvs.vcf.gz``, ``....somatic_indels.vcf.gz``)
    Two fixed columns, ``NORMAL`` and ``TUMOR``. A SNV carries per-base tier-1 counts
    (``AU``, ``CU``, ``GU``, ``TU``): the fraction is the ALT base's count over the four.
    An indel carries ``TIR`` (reads supporting the indel) and ``TAR`` (reads supporting the
    other allele): the fraction is ``TIR / (TIR + TAR)``. Depth is ``DP`` for both.

``muse`` (``<pair>.muse.vcf.gz``)
    Two fixed columns, ``TUMOR`` and ``NORMAL``, FORMAT ``GT:DP:AD:BQ:SS``. Allele fraction
    is ``AD[1] / (AD[0] + AD[1])``. MuSE calls SNVs only and writes its confidence as a FILTER
    tier (``PASS``, ``Tier1`` to ``Tier5``).

A tumour sample called on its own (no matched normal) has one genotype column and is read
like a germline callset: allele fraction from ``AF`` (Mutect2), ``VAF`` or ``AD``. The
paired parsers need a normal, so a pair called by any other caller is left out rather than
guessed at: its genotype columns could be either way round.

Structural-variant callers (Manta, TIDDIT) and gVCFs are not point variants and are left to
their own collections.

The frame holds one row per call with the key ``variant_key`` the germline tables use
(``chrom:pos:ref:alt``), so a somatic call can be matched to a germline one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import defaultdict

import polars as pl

from depictio.recipes.lib.sarek_units import is_pair
from depictio.recipes.lib.vcf import (
    _ANNOTATOR_ANN_SUFFIX_RE,
    _DATA_LINE_RE,
    _VCF_SUFFIX_RE,
    ALLELE_KEY_CHARS,
    RAW_LINE_COL,
    SOURCE_PATH_COL,
    _variant_type,
)

#: The callers whose calls are structural variants, read by ``sv_to_long``.
SV_CALLERS = frozenset({"manta", "tiddit"})
#: The callers a pair is read with.
PAIRED_CALLERS = ("mutect2", "strelka", "muse")

#: Columns every ``somatic_to_long`` frame carries, in order.
SOMATIC_COLUMNS = [
    "unit",
    "caller",
    "chrom",
    "pos",
    "variant_key",
    "ref",
    "alt",
    "variant_type",
    "qual",
    "score",
    "filter_status",
    "is_pass",
    "tumour_vaf",
    "tumour_dp",
    "normal_vaf",
    "normal_dp",
]

SOMATIC_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "unit": pl.Utf8,
    "caller": pl.Utf8,
    "chrom": pl.Utf8,
    "pos": pl.Int64,
    "variant_key": pl.Utf8,
    "ref": pl.Utf8,
    "alt": pl.Utf8,
    "variant_type": pl.Utf8,
    "qual": pl.Float64,
    "score": pl.Float64,
    "filter_status": pl.Utf8,
    "is_pass": pl.Boolean,
    "tumour_vaf": pl.Float64,
    "tumour_dp": pl.Int64,
    "normal_vaf": pl.Float64,
    "normal_dp": pl.Int64,
}

_INFO_SOMATIC_EVS_RE = r"(?:^|;)SomaticEVS=([^;]+)"
_INFO_TLOD_RE = r"(?:^|;)TLOD=([^;,]+)"
_INFO_DP_RE = r"(?:^|;)DP=(\d+)"

#: Column offset of the first genotype column of a VCF.
_FIRST_SAMPLE = 9
#: Out-of-range column index: ``list.get`` answers null for it.
_NO_COLUMN = 999


def _tokens(path: str) -> list[str]:
    """``[unit, caller, qualifier...]`` of a VCF's file name (see ``vcf.sample_and_caller``)."""
    name = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    stem = re.sub(_ANNOTATOR_ANN_SUFFIX_RE, "", re.sub(_VCF_SUFFIX_RE, "", name))
    return stem.split(".")


def _headers(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Per file: its genotype column names and the tumour and normal the header names."""
    info: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(dict)
    lines = raw.filter(pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.starts_with("#")).select(
        RAW_LINE_COL, SOURCE_PATH_COL
    )
    for line, path in zip(
        lines[RAW_LINE_COL].to_list(), lines[SOURCE_PATH_COL].to_list(), strict=True
    ):
        if line.startswith("#CHROM"):
            info[path]["columns"] = line.split("\t")[_FIRST_SAMPLE:]
        elif line.startswith("##tumor_sample="):
            info[path]["tumour"] = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
        elif line.startswith("##normal_sample="):
            info[path]["normal"] = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
    return info


def _index(columns: list[str] | None, name: str | None, default: int) -> int:
    """Position of ``name`` among the genotype columns, ``default`` when the header lacks it."""
    if columns and name:
        lowered = [c.lower() for c in columns]
        if name.lower() in lowered:
            return lowered.index(name.lower())
    return default


def plan_files(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per VCF to read: its unit, caller, parser and tumour and normal column.

    A file no parser covers is not in the plan (and its rows are not in the result).
    ``t_col`` and ``n_col`` are positions among the genotype columns; ``n_col`` is
    ``_NO_COLUMN`` for a tumour on its own.
    """
    headers = _headers(raw)
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for path in raw[SOURCE_PATH_COL].unique().to_list():
        tokens = _tokens(path)
        if len(tokens) < 2:
            continue
        unit, caller, qualifiers = tokens[0], tokens[1].lower(), [t.lower() for t in tokens[2:]]
        if caller in SV_CALLERS or "genome" in qualifiers or "g" in qualifiers:
            continue
        head = headers.get(path, {})
        columns = head.get("columns")
        if is_pair(unit):
            if caller == "mutect2" and "filtered" in qualifiers:
                parser = "mutect2"
                t_col = _index(columns, head.get("tumour"), 1)
                n_col = _index(columns, head.get("normal"), 0)
            elif caller == "strelka" and "somatic_snvs" in qualifiers:
                parser = "strelka_snv"
                t_col, n_col = _index(columns, "TUMOR", 1), _index(columns, "NORMAL", 0)
            elif caller == "strelka" and "somatic_indels" in qualifiers:
                parser = "strelka_indel"
                t_col, n_col = _index(columns, "TUMOR", 1), _index(columns, "NORMAL", 0)
            elif caller == "muse":
                parser = "muse"
                t_col, n_col = _index(columns, "TUMOR", 0), _index(columns, "NORMAL", 1)
            else:
                continue
        else:
            # A tumour on its own: the unfiltered Mutect2 file is the filtered one before its filters.
            if caller == "mutect2" and "filtered" not in qualifiers:
                continue
            parser, t_col, n_col = "single", 0, _NO_COLUMN
        rows.append(
            {
                SOURCE_PATH_COL: path,
                "unit": unit,
                "caller": caller,
                "parser": parser,
                "t_col": t_col,
                "n_col": n_col,
            }
        )
    return pl.DataFrame(
        rows,
        schema={
            SOURCE_PATH_COL: pl.Utf8,
            "unit": pl.Utf8,
            "caller": pl.Utf8,
            "parser": pl.Utf8,
            "t_col": pl.Int64,
            "n_col": pl.Int64,
        },
    )


def _fmt(field: str, key: str) -> pl.Expr:
    """The value of FORMAT key ``key`` in genotype column ``field`` (null when absent)."""
    keys = pl.col("format").str.split(":")
    values = pl.col(field).str.split(":")
    index = keys.list.eval(pl.element() == key).list.arg_max()
    return (
        pl.when(keys.list.contains(key))
        .then(values.list.get(index, null_on_oob=True))
        .otherwise(None)
    )


def _first_number(expr: pl.Expr) -> pl.Expr:
    """The first value of a comma list, as a float (``.`` and absent become null)."""
    return expr.str.split(",").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)


def _ratio(num: pl.Expr, den: pl.Expr) -> pl.Expr:
    return pl.when(den > 0).then(num / den).otherwise(None).cast(pl.Float64)


def _ad_fraction(field: str) -> pl.Expr:
    """``AD[1] / (AD[0] + AD[1])``: the first ALT allele's share of the two allele depths."""
    depths = _fmt(field, "AD").str.split(",")
    ref = depths.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
    alt = depths.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
    return _ratio(alt, ref + alt)


def _depth(field: str) -> pl.Expr:
    return _fmt(field, "DP").cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)


def _evidence(parser: str, field: str) -> tuple[pl.Expr, pl.Expr]:
    """``(allele fraction, depth)`` of one genotype column under one parser."""
    if parser == "strelka_snv":
        counts = {b: _first_number(_fmt(field, f"{b}U")) for b in "ACGT"}
        alt_base = pl.col("alt_first").str.slice(0, 1).str.to_uppercase()
        alt = pl.coalesce(
            *[pl.when(alt_base == base).then(count) for base, count in counts.items()]
        )
        total = counts["A"] + counts["C"] + counts["G"] + counts["T"]
        return _ratio(alt, total), _depth(field)
    if parser == "strelka_indel":
        indel, other = _first_number(_fmt(field, "TIR")), _first_number(_fmt(field, "TAR"))
        return _ratio(indel, indel + other), _depth(field)
    if parser == "mutect2":
        return pl.coalesce(_first_number(_fmt(field, "AF")), _ad_fraction(field)), _depth(field)
    if parser == "muse":
        return _ad_fraction(field), _depth(field)
    # A tumour on its own, whatever the caller: the germline-style fields.
    vaf = pl.coalesce(
        _first_number(_fmt(field, "AF")), _first_number(_fmt(field, "VAF")), _ad_fraction(field)
    )
    depth = pl.coalesce(
        _depth(field), pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_DP_RE, 1).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
    )
    return vaf, depth


def somatic_to_long(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per somatic call, from a raw ``raw_line`` / ``source_path`` frame.

    The frame may hold the VCF header lines (``#``): the genotype column names and the
    ``##tumor_sample=`` / ``##normal_sample=`` lines say which column is the tumour.
    Returns :data:`SOMATIC_COLUMNS`; empty when no file of the frame has a parser.
    """
    plan = plan_files(raw)
    empty = pl.DataFrame(schema=SOMATIC_SCHEMA)
    if plan.is_empty():
        return empty
    data = raw.filter(
        pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).is_not_null() & pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.contains(_DATA_LINE_RE)
    ).join(plan, on=SOURCE_PATH_COL, how="inner")
    if data.is_empty():
        return empty

    fields = pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.split("\t")
    data = data.with_columns(
        fields.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("chrom"),
        fields.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("pos"),
        fields.list.get(3, null_on_oob=True).alias("ref"),
        fields.list.get(4, null_on_oob=True).alias("alt"),
        fields.list.get(5, null_on_oob=True).alias("qual_text"),
        fields.list.get(6, null_on_oob=True).alias("filter_status"),
        fields.list.get(7, null_on_oob=True).alias("info"),
        fields.list.get(8, null_on_oob=True).alias("format"),
        fields.list.get(_FIRST_SAMPLE + pl.col("t_col"), null_on_oob=True).alias("tumour_field"),
        fields.list.get(_FIRST_SAMPLE + pl.col("n_col"), null_on_oob=True).alias("normal_field"),
    ).with_columns(pl.col("alt").str.split(",").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("alt_first"))

    frames: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
    for parser in plan["parser"].unique().to_list():
        part = data.filter(pl.col("parser") == parser)
        t_vaf, t_dp = _evidence(parser, "tumour_field")
        if parser == "single":
            n_vaf, n_dp = pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Float64), pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Int64)
        else:
            n_vaf, n_dp = _evidence(parser, "normal_field")
        frames.append(
            part.with_columns(
                t_vaf.alias("tumour_vaf"),
                t_dp.alias("tumour_dp"),
                n_vaf.alias("normal_vaf"),
                n_dp.alias("normal_dp"),
            )
        )
    out = pl.concat(frames, how="vertical_relaxed")

    qual = pl.col("qual_text").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
    return out.with_columns(
        qual.alias("qual"),
        pl.coalesce(
            pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_SOMATIC_EVS_RE, 1).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False),
            pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_TLOD_RE, 1).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False),
            qual,
        ).alias("score"),
        _variant_type().alias("variant_type"),
        pl.col("filter_status").is_in(["PASS", ".", ""]).alias("is_pass"),
        pl.concat_str(
            [
                pl.col("chrom"),
                pl.col("pos").cast(pl.Utf8),
                pl.col("ref").str.slice(0, ALLELE_KEY_CHARS),
                pl.col("alt_first").str.slice(0, ALLELE_KEY_CHARS),
            ],
            separator=":",
        ).alias("variant_key"),
    ).select(SOMATIC_COLUMNS)


#: The callers that genotype a pair's two samples together, whatever the variant is: their
#: records give the tumour's allele fraction at the sites where the normal is heterozygous.
JOINT_CALLERS = ("freebayes",)

JOINT_SITE_COLUMNS = [
    "unit",
    "chrom",
    "pos",
    "variant_key",
    "ref",
    "alt",
    "normal_vaf",
    "normal_dp",
    "tumour_vaf",
    "tumour_dp",
]

JOINT_SITE_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "unit": pl.Utf8,
    "chrom": pl.Utf8,
    "pos": pl.Int64,
    "variant_key": pl.Utf8,
    "ref": pl.Utf8,
    "alt": pl.Utf8,
    "normal_vaf": pl.Float64,
    "normal_dp": pl.Int64,
    "tumour_vaf": pl.Float64,
    "tumour_dp": pl.Int64,
}

_HET_GENOTYPES = ("0/1", "0|1", "1/0", "1|0")


def _joint_plan(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per jointly-genotyped pair file: its unit and the tumour and normal columns.

    The genotype columns are named after the sample (``<patient>_<sample>`` on sarek), so the
    tumour and the normal are the columns whose name ends with the pair's sample names; a file
    whose header names neither falls back to sarek's order, normal first.
    """
    headers = _headers(raw)
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for path in raw[SOURCE_PATH_COL].unique().to_list():
        tokens = _tokens(path)
        if len(tokens) < 2 or not is_pair(tokens[0]) or tokens[1].lower() not in JOINT_CALLERS:
            continue
        if any(t.lower() in ("genome", "g") for t in tokens[2:]):
            continue
        tumour, _, normal = tokens[0].partition("_vs_")
        columns = [c.lower() for c in headers.get(path, {}).get("columns") or []]

        def find(name: str, default: int, columns: list[str] = columns) -> int:
            hits = [i for i, c in enumerate(columns) if c.endswith(name.lower())]
            return hits[0] if hits else default

        rows.append(
            {
                SOURCE_PATH_COL: path,
                "unit": tokens[0],
                "t_col": find(tumour, 1),
                "n_col": find(normal, 0),
            }
        )
    return pl.DataFrame(
        rows,
        schema={
            SOURCE_PATH_COL: pl.Utf8,
            "unit": pl.Utf8,
            "t_col": pl.Int64,
            "n_col": pl.Int64,
        },
    )


def joint_het_sites(raw: pl.DataFrame, *, min_depth: int = 10) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The pair's heterozygous germline SNVs, with the allele fraction in both samples.

    A caller that genotypes the tumour and its normal together (Freebayes) writes both
    columns on every record. Keeps the single-nucleotide records whose *normal* genotype is
    heterozygous and whose two depths reach ``min_depth``: at such a site the normal's
    allele fraction sits near 0.5, and a tumour that has lost one parental copy (LOH) or
    gained one shows it as a fraction away from 0.5. Returns :data:`JOINT_SITE_COLUMNS`,
    empty when no file of the frame is a jointly genotyped pair.
    """
    plan = _joint_plan(raw)
    empty = pl.DataFrame(schema=JOINT_SITE_SCHEMA)
    if plan.is_empty():
        return empty
    data = raw.filter(
        pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).is_not_null() & pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.contains(_DATA_LINE_RE)
    ).join(plan, on=SOURCE_PATH_COL, how="inner")
    if data.is_empty():
        return empty
    fields = pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.split("\t")
    data = data.with_columns(
        fields.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("chrom"),
        fields.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("pos"),
        fields.list.get(3, null_on_oob=True).alias("ref"),
        fields.list.get(4, null_on_oob=True).str.split(",").list.get(0).alias("alt"),
        fields.list.get(8, null_on_oob=True).alias("format"),
        fields.list.get(_FIRST_SAMPLE + pl.col("t_col"), null_on_oob=True).alias("tumour_field"),
        fields.list.get(_FIRST_SAMPLE + pl.col("n_col"), null_on_oob=True).alias("normal_field"),
    ).filter(pl.col("ref").str.len_chars() == 1, pl.col("alt").str.len_chars() == 1)
    out = data.with_columns(
        _fmt("normal_field", "GT").alias("_normal_gt"),
        _ad_fraction("normal_field").alias("normal_vaf"),
        _depth("normal_field").alias("normal_dp"),
        _ad_fraction("tumour_field").alias("tumour_vaf"),
        _depth("tumour_field").alias("tumour_dp"),
    ).filter(
        pl.col("_normal_gt").is_in(_HET_GENOTYPES),
        pl.col("normal_dp") >= min_depth,
        pl.col("tumour_dp") >= min_depth,
        pl.col("tumour_vaf").is_not_null(),
        pl.col("normal_vaf").is_not_null(),
    )
    return (
        out.with_columns(
            pl.concat_str(
                [pl.col("chrom"), pl.col("pos").cast(pl.Utf8), pl.col("ref"), pl.col("alt")],
                separator=":",
            ).alias("variant_key")
        )
        .unique(subset=["unit", "variant_key"], keep="first", maintain_order=True)
        .select(JOINT_SITE_COLUMNS)
    )


#: snpEff's impact classes, worst first as a rank (an unknown class ranks 0).
IMPACT_RANK = {"HIGH": 4, "MODERATE": 3, "LOW": 2, "MODIFIER": 1}

ANNOTATION_BY_VARIANT_SCHEMA: dict[str, type[pl.DataType]] = {
    "unit": pl.Utf8,
    "variant_key": pl.Utf8,
    "gene": pl.Utf8,
    "gene_id": pl.Utf8,
    "impact": pl.Utf8,
    "consequence": pl.Utf8,
    "hgvs_p": pl.Utf8,
    "aa_pos": pl.Int64,
}

_ANN_FIELD_INFO_RE = r"(?:^|;)ANN=([^;\t]+)"
_ANN_PROTEIN_POS_RE = r"p\.[A-Za-z]{3}(\d+)"
#: Index of the transcript biotype in an ANN entry.
_ANN_BIOTYPE = 7


def annotation_by_variant(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The worst snpEff annotation of each variant of each unit, from annotated VCF lines.

    snpEff writes one ``ANN`` entry per overlapping transcript. A somatic call is read by its
    worst consequence: the entry with the highest impact class, a protein-coding transcript
    before another biotype and the file's own order after that. A variant several callers
    made is annotated once (the annotation does not depend on the caller). One row per
    ``(unit, variant_key)``, :data:`ANNOTATION_BY_VARIANT_SCHEMA`.
    """
    empty = pl.DataFrame(schema=ANNOTATION_BY_VARIANT_SCHEMA)
    fields = pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.split("\t")
    records = (
        raw.filter(
            pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).is_not_null() & pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.contains(_DATA_LINE_RE)
        )
        .with_columns(
            fields.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("chrom"),
            fields.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).alias("pos"),
            fields.list.get(3, null_on_oob=True).alias("ref"),
            fields.list.get(4, null_on_oob=True).str.split(",").list.get(0).alias("alt_first"),
            fields.list.get(7, null_on_oob=True).alias("info"),
        )
        .join(
            _unit_of_path(raw),
            on=SOURCE_PATH_COL,
            how="left",
        )
    )
    if records.is_empty():
        return empty
    entries = (
        records.with_columns(
            pl.concat_str(
                [
                    pl.col("chrom"),
                    pl.col("pos"),
                    pl.col("ref").str.slice(0, ALLELE_KEY_CHARS),
                    pl.col("alt_first").str.slice(0, ALLELE_KEY_CHARS),
                ],
                separator=":",
            ).alias("variant_key"),
            pl.col("info").str.extract(_ANN_FIELD_INFO_RE, 1).str.split(",").alias("_ann"),
        )
        .select("unit", "variant_key", "_ann")
        # A record with no ANN explodes to a null row on polars < 2; dropped below
        # (the CI polars has no `empty_as_null`).
        .explode("_ann")
        .drop_nulls("_ann")
        .with_row_index("_order")
    )
    parts = pl.col("_ann").str.split("|")
    parsed = entries.with_columns(
        parts.list.get(2, null_on_oob=True).alias("impact"),
        parts.list.get(3, null_on_oob=True).alias("gene"),
        parts.list.get(4, null_on_oob=True).alias("gene_id"),
        parts.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).str.split("&").list.get(0).alias("consequence"),
        parts.list.get(10, null_on_oob=True).alias("hgvs_p"),
        (parts.list.get(_ANN_BIOTYPE, null_on_oob=True) == "protein_coding").alias("_coding"),
    ).with_columns(
        pl.col("impact")
        .replace_strict(IMPACT_RANK, default=0, return_dtype=pl.Int64)
        .alias("_rank")
    )
    worst = (
        parsed.sort(["_rank", "_coding", "_order"], descending=[True, True, False])
        .unique(subset=["unit", "variant_key"], keep="first", maintain_order=True)
        .with_columns(
            *[
                pl.when(pl.col(c) == "").then(None).otherwise(pl.col(c)).alias(c)
                for c in ("gene", "gene_id", "hgvs_p")
            ],
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("hgvs_p")
            .str.extract(_ANN_PROTEIN_POS_RE, 1)
            .cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
            .alias("aa_pos")
        )
    )
    return worst.select(list(ANNOTATION_BY_VARIANT_SCHEMA))


def _unit_of_path(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """``source_path`` -> ``unit`` (the first token of the file name, annotator suffix removed)."""
    paths = raw.select(SOURCE_PATH_COL).unique()
    names = [_tokens(p)[0] for p in paths[SOURCE_PATH_COL].to_list()]
    return pl.DataFrame(
        {SOURCE_PATH_COL: paths[SOURCE_PATH_COL].to_list(), "unit": names},
        schema={SOURCE_PATH_COL: pl.Utf8, "unit": pl.Utf8},
    )
files.depictio/recipes/lib/vcf.py:
"""Read a bgzipped VCF into a long per-variant frame with Polars alone.

No pipeline in this repo ships a VCF reader dependency (no cyvcf2, no pysam, no
bcftools binary), and every variant-level panel a variant-calling template wants
(per-caller concordance, VAF against depth, a lollipop along a gene, a rainfall
plot) needs one row per variant. bgzip is gzip-compatible, so Polars reads a
``.vcf.gz`` with its own decompressor and the whole reader is three regexes and
a list index.

The raw DC scans with a separator that never occurs in a VCF (``\\x1e``), so one
full line lands in a single ``raw_line`` text column. That sidesteps two traps a
tab-separated scan walks into:

* a VCF's last column is named after the sample, and nf-core writes that name
  differently per caller (``NA12878_75M`` for DeepVariant,
  ``NA12878_75M_NA12878_75M`` for GATK, Manta and Strelka), so a header-based
  scan across a run's files has no single schema;
* a truncated or dangling object in the bucket (sarek's megatest publishes two
  FreeBayes VCFs as a 196-byte Fusion symlink target, see the template's
  VALIDATION_REPORT) is one junk line here instead of a scan that raises.

Both ids come off the file NAME, ``<sample>.<caller>[.<qualifier>]...vcf.gz``,
which is the only place that survives the layouts the calls are published under
(``variant_calling/<caller>/<sample>/`` in the megatest, ``<sample>/<caller>/``
in sarek's own docs, flat elsewhere). Same rule as
``depictio.recipes.lib.bcftools_stats``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import polars as pl

#: Column holding one full VCF line (see the module docstring for why).
RAW_LINE_COL = "raw_line"
#: Column carrying the VCF's path (``include_file_paths`` on the raw DC).
SOURCE_PATH_COL = "source_path"

#: Longest REF/ALT allele kept inside ``variant_key``. A Manta deletion carries a
#: 335-base REF; the key exists to match a variant across callers, not to store
#: the allele, and the frame keeps ``ref``/``alt`` in full anyway.
ALLELE_KEY_CHARS = 20

_VCF_SUFFIX_RE = r"\.(?:vcf|bcf)(?:\.b?gz)?$"
#: The annotator an nf-core pipeline appends to the caller's own file-name
#: token (``deepvariant_snpEff``, ``haplotypecaller.filtered_VEP``), on the
#: stem itself and on the ``.ann`` sidecar the annotated call is published with.
_ANNOTATOR = r"(?:snpEff|snpeff|VEP|vep)"
_ANNOTATOR_SUFFIX_RE = rf"_{_ANNOTATOR}$"
_ANNOTATOR_ANN_SUFFIX_RE = rf"_{_ANNOTATOR}\.ann$"
#: A data line starts with a contig name and a numeric POS.
_DATA_LINE_RE = r"^[^\t]+\t\d+\t"
#: snpEff writes its per-variant annotations into an ``ANN=`` INFO key.
_ANN_INFO_RE = r"(?:^|;)ANN=([^;\t]+)"
_INFO_DP_RE = r"(?:^|;)DP=(\d+)"
#: Structural-variant INFO keys (VCF 4.2 / Manta / TIDDIT). ``SVLEN`` may be a
#: comma list on a multi-ALT record; the first value is the first ALT's.
_INFO_SVTYPE_RE = r"(?:^|;)SVTYPE=([^;]+)"
_INFO_END_RE = r"(?:^|;)END=(\d+)"
_INFO_SVLEN_RE = r"(?:^|;)SVLEN=(-?\d+)"
_INFO_MATEID_RE = r"(?:^|;)MATEID=([^;,]+)"
_INFO_IMPRECISE_RE = r"(?:^|;)IMPRECISE(?:;|$)"
#: A breakend ALT names the mate locus: ``A]chr22:29769937]`` or ``[chr22:29767384[CG``.
_BND_MATE_RE = r"[\[\]]([^:\[\]]+):(\d+)[\[\]]"
#: ``p.Arg123Gly`` / ``p.Ter45*`` -> 123 / 45.
_HGVS_P_POS_RE = r"p\.[A-Za-z]{3}(\d+)"


def sample_and_caller(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per ``source_path`` with the ``sample`` and ``caller`` it holds.

    Join the result back onto the raw frame on ``source_path``.
    """
    stem = (
        pl.col(SOURCE_PATH_COL)
        .str.split("/")
        .list.last()
        .str.replace(_VCF_SUFFIX_RE, "")
        # Annotated calls keep the caller in the stem but append the annotator:
        # NA12878_75M.haplotypecaller.filtered_snpEff.ann -> ...filtered.
        .str.replace(_ANNOTATOR_ANN_SUFFIX_RE, "")
    )
    tokens = stem.str.split(".")
    # DeepVariant's calls carry no qualifier, so the annotator lands on the
    # caller token itself (NA12878_75M.deepvariant_snpEff.genes.txt) where the
    # other callers keep it on a third one (....filtered_snpEff.genes.txt).
    caller = tokens.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).str.replace(_ANNOTATOR_SUFFIX_RE, "")
    return (
        raw.select(pl.col(SOURCE_PATH_COL))
        .unique()
        .with_columns(
            tokens.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("sample"),
            pl.coalesce(caller, pl.lit("unknown")).alias("caller"),
        )
    )


def _format_value(key: str) -> pl.Expr:
    """The value of FORMAT key ``key`` in the per-sample genotype column.

    FORMAT key order differs per caller (DeepVariant ``GT:GQ:DP:AD:VAF:PL``,
    GATK ``GT:AD:DP:GQ:PL``, Manta ``GT:FT:GQ:PL:PR`` with no depth at all), so
    the key is located in the FORMAT list and the same index read off the
    genotype list rather than assumed.
    """
    keys = pl.col("format").str.split(":")
    values = pl.col("sample_field").str.split(":")
    index = keys.list.eval(pl.element() == key).list.arg_max()
    return (
        pl.when(keys.list.contains(key))
        .then(values.list.get(index, null_on_oob=True))
        .otherwise(None)
    )


def _variant_type() -> pl.Expr:
    """SNP / MNP / INDEL / SV from the first ALT allele."""
    ref = pl.col("ref")
    alt = pl.col("alt_first")
    return (
        pl.when(alt.str.starts_with("<") | alt.str.contains(r"[\[\]]"))
        .then(pl.lit("SV"))
        .when((ref.str.len_chars() == 1) & (alt.str.len_chars() == 1))
        .then(pl.lit("SNP"))
        .when(ref.str.len_chars() == alt.str.len_chars())
        .then(pl.lit("MNP"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("INDEL"))
    )


#: Columns every ``vcf_to_long`` frame carries, in order.
CORE_COLUMNS = [
    "sample",
    "caller",
    "chrom",
    "pos",
    "variant_key",
    "ref",
    "alt",
    "variant_type",
    "qual",
    "filter_status",
    "is_pass",
    "gt",
    "dp",
    "vaf",
]
#: Extra columns ``vcf_to_long(..., with_annotation=True)`` adds.
ANNOTATION_COLUMNS = ["gene", "gene_id", "impact", "consequence", "hgvs_p", "aa_pos"]


def finite_float(column: str) -> pl.Expr:
    """Cast to Float64, turning vcftools' ``-nan`` into a null rather than a NaN.

    vcftools writes ``-nan`` for a ratio with an empty denominator (a Ts/Tv
    over zero transversions); ``strict=False`` reads it as NaN, which is not
    JSON and sorts above every real value, so it is nulled here.
    """
    value = pl.col(column).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
    return pl.when(value.is_finite()).then(value).otherwise(None)


def _split_records(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The data lines of a raw frame split into their VCF columns, with sample and caller."""
    fields = pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.split("\t")
    return (
        raw.filter(
            pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).is_not_null() & pl.col(RAW_LINE_COL).str.contains(_DATA_LINE_RE)
        )
        .with_columns(
            fields.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("chrom"),
            fields.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("pos"),
            fields.list.get(2, null_on_oob=True).alias("record_id"),
            fields.list.get(3, null_on_oob=True).alias("ref"),
            fields.list.get(4, null_on_oob=True).alias("alt"),
            fields.list.get(5, null_on_oob=True).alias("qual_text"),
            fields.list.get(6, null_on_oob=True).alias("filter_status"),
            fields.list.get(7, null_on_oob=True).alias("info"),
            fields.list.get(8, null_on_oob=True).alias("format"),
            fields.list.get(9, null_on_oob=True).alias("sample_field"),
        )
        .join(sample_and_caller(raw), on=SOURCE_PATH_COL, how="left")
    )


#: Columns every ``sv_to_long`` frame carries, in order.
SV_COLUMNS = [
    "sample",
    "caller",
    "chrom",
    "pos",
    "end",
    "svtype",
    "svlen",
    "size_bp",
    "qual",
    "filter_status",
    "is_pass",
    "imprecise",
    "primary",
    "mate_chrom",
    "mate_pos",
]


def sv_to_long(raw: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per structural-variant record, from a raw ``raw_line`` / ``source_path`` frame.

    Reads the INFO keys structural-variant callers write (Manta, TIDDIT):

    * ``svtype``: ``SVTYPE`` (DEL, DUP, INS, INV, BND...), else the ``<TYPE>`` of a
      symbolic ALT, else BND for a breakend ALT;
    * ``end``: ``END``; else ``pos`` plus ``|SVLEN|`` for a DEL, DUP, INV or CNV;
      the position itself for an INS; null for a BND, which has two loci;
    * ``svlen`` / ``size_bp``: ``SVLEN`` (negative for a deletion) and its absolute
      value; null when the caller wrote none (a BND). ``CIPOS`` is not read: an
      imprecise record is flagged by ``imprecise`` alone;
    * ``mate_chrom`` / ``mate_pos``: the other breakend of a BND ALT;
    * ``primary``: one record per event. A BND is two records that name each
      other with ``MATEID``; the one whose ID sorts first is primary, so a count of
      events keeps one side of each pair. Every other record is primary.

    Records are kept as written (both sides of a BND are rows), so a count of
    rows is a count of records; filter on ``primary`` for events. Nothing here
    changes ``vcf_to_long``: a small-variant frame has no ``SVTYPE`` and the
    columns above come out null.
    """
    df = _split_records(raw)
    alt_first = pl.col("alt").str.split(",").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True)
    symbolic = alt_first.str.extract(r"^<([A-Za-z]+)", 1).str.to_uppercase()
    breakend = alt_first.str.contains(r"[\[\]]")
    svtype = pl.coalesce(
        pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_SVTYPE_RE, 1),
        symbolic,
        pl.when(breakend).then(pl.lit("BND")),
    )
    df = df.with_columns(
        svtype.alias("svtype"),
        pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_SVLEN_RE, 1).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("svlen"),
        pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_END_RE, 1).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("_end"),
        pl.col("qual_text").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).alias("qual"),
        pl.col("info").str.contains(_INFO_IMPRECISE_RE).alias("imprecise"),
        pl.col("alt").str.extract(_BND_MATE_RE, 1).alias("mate_chrom"),
        pl.col("alt").str.extract(_BND_MATE_RE, 2).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("mate_pos"),
        pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_MATEID_RE, 1).alias("_mate_id"),
    ).with_columns(
        pl.col("svlen").abs().alias("size_bp"),
        pl.when(pl.col("svtype") == "INS")
        .then(pl.coalesce(pl.col("_end"), pl.col("pos")))
        .when(pl.col("svtype") == "BND")
        .then(pl.col("_end"))
        .otherwise(
            pl.coalesce(
                pl.col("_end"),
                pl.when(pl.col("svlen").is_not_null()).then(pl.col("pos") + pl.col("svlen").abs()),
            )
        )
        .alias("end"),
        pl.col("filter_status").is_in(["PASS", ".", ""]).alias("is_pass"),
        (
            pl.col("_mate_id").is_null()
            | pl.col("record_id").is_null()
            | (pl.col("record_id") <= pl.col("_mate_id"))
        ).alias("primary"),
    )
    return df.select(SV_COLUMNS)


def vcf_to_long(raw: pl.DataFrame, *, with_annotation: bool = False) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per variant call, from a raw ``raw_line`` / ``source_path`` frame.

    ``with_annotation`` additionally splits snpEff's first ``ANN`` entry into
    gene, impact, consequence and protein change. snpEff emits one ANN entry per
    overlapping transcript, ordered by severity, so the first entry is the
    canonical "worst consequence" the summary reports are built on.

    ``vaf`` is the first ALT allele's fraction: the caller's own ``VAF`` field
    when it writes one, else ``AD[1] / (AD[0] + AD[1])``, which leaves the
    remaining alt depths of a multi-allelic record out of both numerator and
    denominator. That is the same first-ALT convention ``variant_type`` and
    ``variant_key`` follow, so the three columns describe one allele.
    """
    df = _split_records(raw)

    allele_depths = _format_value("AD").str.split(",")
    ad_ref = allele_depths.list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
    ad_alt = allele_depths.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)

    df = df.with_columns(
        pl.col("alt").str.split(",").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True).alias("alt_first"),
        pl.col("qual_text").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).alias("qual"),
        _format_value("GT").alias("gt"),
        pl.coalesce(
            _format_value("DP").cast(pl.Int64, strict=False),
            pl.col("info").str.extract(_INFO_DP_RE, 1).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False),
        ).alias("dp"),
        pl.coalesce(
            _format_value("VAF").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False),
            pl.when((ad_ref + ad_alt) > 0).then(ad_alt / (ad_ref + ad_alt)).otherwise(None),
        ).alias("vaf"),
    ).with_columns(
        _variant_type().alias("variant_type"),
        # PASS is spelled "PASS" by every caller here; Strelka and GATK also
        # write a semicolon-joined list of failed filters, and DeepVariant
        # writes "." when it applied none.
        pl.col("filter_status").is_in(["PASS", ".", ""]).alias("is_pass"),
        pl.concat_str(
            [
                pl.col("chrom"),
                pl.col("pos").cast(pl.Utf8),
                pl.col("ref").str.slice(0, ALLELE_KEY_CHARS),
                pl.col("alt_first").str.slice(0, ALLELE_KEY_CHARS),
            ],
            separator=":",
        ).alias("variant_key"),
    )

    if not with_annotation:
        return df.select(CORE_COLUMNS)

    ann = pl.col("info").str.extract(_ANN_INFO_RE, 1).str.split(",").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True)
    ann_fields = ann.str.split("|")
    df = df.with_columns(
        ann_fields.list.get(3, null_on_oob=True).alias("gene"),
        ann_fields.list.get(4, null_on_oob=True).alias("gene_id"),
        ann_fields.list.get(2, null_on_oob=True).alias("impact"),
        # snpEff joins co-occurring consequences with "&"; the first one is the
        # most severe and is what every summary counts.
        ann_fields.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True)
        .str.split("&")
        .list.get(0, null_on_oob=True)
        .alias("consequence"),
        ann_fields.list.get(10, null_on_oob=True).alias("hgvs_p"),
    ).with_columns(
        pl.col("hgvs_p").str.extract(_HGVS_P_POS_RE, 1).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False).alias("aa_pos")
    )
    return df.select(CORE_COLUMNS + ANNOTATION_COLUMNS)
files.depictio/recipes/lib/viralmetagenome.py:
"""Shared parsing for the nf-core/viralmetagenome outputs.

The pipeline names every per-sample output after the sample and, for a mapping,
after the reference the reads went to, and prefixes all of it with the run's
``--global_prefix`` (``<prefix>_<date>_<version>_<run name>-``):

* a mapping against a constraint reference:
  ``[<prefix>-]<sample>_<reference>-CONSTRAINT_constraint.<ext>``
  (CheckV writes the folder ``<sample>_<reference>-CONSTRAINT``);
* a de novo consensus, at one step of its refinement:
  ``[<prefix>-]<sample>_<cluster>_it<N>.<ext>``, ``..._consensus``, or
  ``..._itvariant-calling``.

The overview tables (``overview-tables/[<prefix>-]*_overview.tsv``) are the
pipeline's own merge of its MultiQC sections: one row per sample, or per
consensus genome, and one column per ``(<tool>) <metric>`` the report holds,
named the way MultiQC labels it.

Everything here keys a genome the same way, ``<sample>_<reference>``, so the
consensus, variant and coverage collections join on ``genome_id``.

Shared here rather than copied because several recipes split the same names,
and recipes may not import one another.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable

import polars as pl

ROUTE_CONSTRAINT = "constraint"
ROUTE_DENOVO = "de novo"

# The reads are mapped to a constraint reference (`-CONSTRAINT`, `_constraint`)
# or to a de novo consensus; the step suffix says how far the refinement went.
_CONSTRAINT = re.compile(r"-CONSTRAINT(?:_constraint)?$|_constraint$")
_STEP = re.compile(r"_(it\d+|itvariant-calling|consensus)$")
_TOOL_TAIL = re.compile(r"\.consensus(?:_[A-Za-z0-9]+)?$")


def run_prefix_free(name: str, sample: str) -> str:
    """``name`` from the first occurrence of ``sample`` on, the run prefix dropped.

    ``test_20260916_1.2.0_run-S1_cl0_it1`` with sample ``S1`` reads ``S1_cl0_it1``.
    A name that does not hold the sample is returned unchanged.
    """
    at = name.find(sample) if sample else -1
    return name[at:] if at >= 0 else name


def split_mapping_name(name: str, sample: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None]:
    """``(reference, route, step)`` of a per-mapping output name.

    ``name`` is a file stem (or folder) without its extension, e.g.
    ``<prefix>-S1_REF-CONSTRAINT_constraint``, ``S1_cl0_it1``,
    ``S1_REF-CONSTRAINT_itvariant-calling.consensus_ivar``. The reference is the
    constraint id or the de novo cluster id; the step is null for a constraint
    mapping and for a name without one. A name that is the sample alone has no
    reference.
    """
    rest = run_prefix_free(name, sample)
    if sample and rest.startswith(sample):
        rest = rest[len(sample) :]
    rest = _TOOL_TAIL.sub("", rest.lstrip("_-"))
    if not rest:
        return None, None, None
    step: str | None = None
    m = _STEP.search(rest)
    if m:
        step = m.group(1)
        rest = rest[: m.start()]
    if _CONSTRAINT.search(rest) or rest.endswith("-CONSTRAINT"):
        reference = _CONSTRAINT.sub("", rest).removesuffix("-CONSTRAINT")
        return reference or None, ROUTE_CONSTRAINT, step
    return rest or None, ROUTE_DENOVO, step


def genome_id(sample: str | None, reference: str | None) -> str | None:
    """The key every per-genome collection joins on: ``<sample>_<reference>``."""
    if sample is None:
        return None
    return f"{sample}_{reference}" if reference else sample


def sample_from_path(path: str, generic_dirs: Iterable[str] = ()) -> str:
    """The per-sample folder a file sits in, or its stem when it sits in a tool folder.

    viralmetagenome writes ``<tool>/<sample>/<file>``; a flat layout
    (``<tool>/<file>``) has no sample folder, and the stem then names the sample.
    """
    parts = path.replace("\\", "/").split("/")
    stem = parts[-1]
    parent = parts[-2] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    if parent and parent not in set(generic_dirs) and parent in stem:
        return parent
    return stem


def strip_extensions(name: str, extensions: Iterable[str]) -> str:
    """``name`` without the first of ``extensions`` it ends with."""
    for ext in extensions:
        if name.endswith(ext):
            return name[: -len(ext)]
    return name


def num(df: pl.DataFrame, column: str, dtype: type[pl.DataType] = pl.Float64) -> pl.Expr:
    """``column`` cast to ``dtype`` (text values like ``NA`` become null), or a null column."""
    if column not in df.columns:
        return pl.lit(None, dtype=dtype)
    expr = pl.col(column).cast(pl.Utf8).str.strip_chars()
    if dtype == pl.Int64:
        return expr.cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).round(0).cast(pl.Int64)
    return expr.cast(dtype, strict=False)


def text(df: pl.DataFrame, column: str) -> pl.Expr:
    """``column`` as stripped text with empty, ``NA`` and ``None`` values null."""
    if column not in df.columns:
        return pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8)
    value = pl.col(column).cast(pl.Utf8).str.strip_chars()
    return (
        pl.when(value.is_in(["", "NA", "N/A", "None", "nan", "null"])).then(None).otherwise(value)
    )


def first_present(
    df: pl.DataFrame, *columns: str, dtype: type[pl.DataType] = pl.Float64
) -> pl.Expr:
    """The first non-null of ``columns`` that the frame has, cast to ``dtype``."""
    present = [num(df, c, dtype) for c in columns if c in df.columns]
    if not present:
        return pl.lit(None, dtype=dtype)
    return pl.coalesce(present)


def as_percent(expr: pl.Expr) -> pl.Expr:
    """A share written as a fraction (0 to 1) read as a percentage.

    MultiQC's general statistics hold fastp's Q30 and GC rates and the annotation
    identity as fractions; a value above 1 is already a percentage.
    """
    return pl.when(expr <= 1.0).then(expr * 100.0).otherwise(expr)


def sanitise(name: str) -> str:
    """A column name every downstream store accepts: letters, digits and underscores."""
    return re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z]+", "_", name.strip()).strip("_").lower() or "column"

# Placeholder strings a missing annotation is written with.
_UNNAMED = ["", "NA", "N/A", "None", "nan", "null", "-"]


def _first_text(df: pl.DataFrame, columns: tuple[str, ...]) -> pl.Expr:
    present = [text(df, c) for c in columns if c in df.columns]
    return pl.coalesce(present) if present else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Utf8)


def tidy_genome_overview(df: pl.DataFrame, default_route: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per consensus genome of a ``*_overview.tsv`` table, in GENOME_SCHEMA.

    ``default_route`` is the route the table holds (``constraint`` for the
    mapping overview, ``de novo`` for the contig overviews); a row whose step is
    ``constraint`` is a constraint mapping either way.
    """
    if df.is_empty():
        return pl.DataFrame(schema=GENOME_SCHEMA)
    out = df.select(
        text(df, "sample").alias("sample"),
        text(df, "cluster").alias("reference"),
        text(df, "step").alias("step"),
        *[
            first_present(df, *cols, dtype=dtype).alias(c)
            for c, (cols, dtype) in GENOME_NUMERIC.items()
        ],
        *[_first_text(df, cols).alias(c) for c, cols in GENOME_TEXT.items()],
    )
    out = out.filter(pl.col("sample").is_not_null())
    route = (
        pl.when(pl.col("step") == ROUTE_CONSTRAINT)
        .then(pl.lit(ROUTE_CONSTRAINT))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(default_route))
    )
    out = out.with_columns(
        route.alias("route"),
        pl.when(pl.col("step") == ROUTE_CONSTRAINT)
        .then(None)
        .otherwise(pl.col("step"))
        .alias("step"),
        as_percent(pl.col("annotation_identity_pct")).round(2).alias("annotation_identity_pct"),
        as_percent(pl.col("dup_pct")).round(3).alias("dup_pct"),
        pl.when(pl.col("consensus_length") > 0)
        .then((pl.col("blast_aligned_bp") * 100.0 / pl.col("consensus_length")).round(2))
        .otherwise(None)
        .alias("blast_query_cover_pct"),
    )
    virus = pl.coalesce(
        [
            pl.when(pl.col(c).is_in(_UNNAMED)).then(None).otherwise(pl.col(c))
            for c in ("annotation_acronym", "annotation_name", "constraint_species")
        ]
    )
    out = out.with_columns(
        virus.fill_null("Unclassified").alias("virus"),
        pl.struct("sample", "reference")
        .map_elements(lambda r: genome_id(r["sample"], r["reference"]), return_dtype=pl.Utf8)
        .alias("genome_id"),
    )
    return out.select([pl.col(c).cast(t) for c, t in GENOME_SCHEMA.items()])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run prefix and assembler names
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# `--global_prefix` reads `<prefix>_<yyyymmdd>_<version>_<run name>`, and the
# pipeline joins it to every file name with a dash.
_GLOBAL_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^[^-/]*_\d{8}_[^_/-]+_[^/-]+-")


def strip_global_prefix(name: str) -> str:
    """``name`` without the run's ``--global_prefix`` and its dash, when it has one."""
    return _GLOBAL_PREFIX.sub("", name, count=1)


_CONTIG_SIZE = re.compile(r"\|size(\d+)$")
_ASSEMBLER = re.compile(r"^(?P<asm>[A-Za-z0-9]+?)_(?:scaffold|contig|NODE|k\d+|TRINITY)", re.I)


def contig_assembler(contig: str) -> str | None:
    """The assembler a de novo contig id names (``megahit_scaffold3|size476`` reads megahit)."""
    m = _ASSEMBLER.match(contig or "")
    return m.group("asm").lower() if m else None


def contig_size(contig: str) -> int | None:
    """The length a contig id carries after ``|size``, else null."""
    m = _CONTIG_SIZE.search(contig or "")
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None

# Design columns
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: Column ``GROUP_COL`` resolves to when the run gives no design table.
NO_GROUP_COL = "__no_group__"
NO_GROUP_VALUE = "All samples"


def design_columns(metadata: pl.DataFrame | None, reserved: set[str]) -> pl.DataFrame | None:
    """The design table keyed on ``sample``, every other column as Delta-safe text.

    The sample id sits in the column named ``sample`` or, failing that, the
    first column; a column whose safe name would replace a reserved one (a
    measure of the hub) is left out.
    """
    if metadata is None or metadata.is_empty() or metadata.width < 2:
        return None
    id_col = "sample" if "sample" in metadata.columns else metadata.columns[0]
    keep: dict[str, str] = {}
    for col in metadata.columns:
        if col == id_col:
            continue
        safe = re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z]+", "_", col.strip()).strip("_") or "column"
        if safe in reserved or safe in keep.values():
            continue
        keep[col] = safe
    if not keep:
        return None
    return (
        metadata.select(
            pl.col(id_col).cast(pl.Utf8).str.strip_chars().alias("sample"),
            *[pl.col(c).cast(pl.Utf8).alias(s) for c, s in keep.items()],
        )
        .filter(pl.col("sample").is_not_null())
        .unique(subset="sample", keep="first")
    )
